questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following periods is also known as Chalcolithic Age?
questions.explanation: Copper Age is also known as the Chalcolithic age. The age in which instruments of copper were used in addition to stone, is called Copper Age.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Indus Civilization existed in:
questions.explanation: The Historical period is determined with respect to the available written literature. The period before which knowledge of the art of writing was not available is called early historical age. Indus Civilization is a Proto-historical civilization although the writing was known during this period, it is still to be deciphered.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest evidence of animal domestication and agriculture in India has come from:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mehrgarh is a Neolithic site located near the Bolan Pass on the Karachi Plain of Balochistan (Pakistan) to the west of the Indus River valley. The earliest evidence of animal domestication and agriculture in British India has come from Mehrgarh. While based on of the latest discoveries, the site with the oldest evidence of agriculture in the Indian subcontinent is Lahuradev (Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which colour was commonly used in the Harappan Pottery?
questions.explanation: The Harappan pottery is bright or dark red and uniformly sturdy and well-baked. It consists of wheel-made wares, both plain and painted. The plain ware is usually of red clay with or without a fi ne red slip. The painted pottery was of red and black colours. Several methods were used by people for the decoration of pottery. Polychrome pottery was rare and mainly comprised small vases decorated with geometric patterns, mostly in red, black and green and less frequently in white and yellow. The colour- scheme adopted for painting was light black, chocolate or light red over buff or greenish-buff background.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following Harappan cities, furrows of ploughed fi elds have been found?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kalibangan town is located on the bank of Ghaggar River (Saraswati River) in Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan. Kalibangan has given the evidence of the earliest plowed agricultural fi eld ever revealed through excavation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following Harappan sites terracotta of 'plough' was found?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Banawali is located in Fatehabad district of Haryana where a terracotta replica of plough was found.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the most signifi cant feature of the Indus Valley Civilization?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The use of burnt bricks in the construction of buildings was one of the main features of the Indus Valley Civilization. Burnt bricks were used in abundance in Harappa and Mohenjo Daro. In Lothal, burnt bricks were used in the construction of drainage. Well planned architecture, advanced trade and commerce were other main feature of this civilisation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following animals was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.explanation: Among the given options evidence of cow and elephant have been found. A seal of zebu bull has been found. Seals depicting elephant has also been found. There is some dispute regarding horse but latest excavation has revealed the evidence of horse. However Horse did not play any major role during Indus Valley Civilisation. BPSC has accepted (b) as correct answer.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following was not associated with the excavation of Harappa and Mohenjodaro?
questions.explanation: In 1921, Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa. In 1926-27 and 1933-34, M.S. Vats was associated with the excavation of Harappa. MohenjoDaro was discovered in 1922 by Rakhal Das Banerjee. In addition to him, some other scholars like K.N. Dixit, Ernest Mackay, Aurel Stein, A. Ghosh and J.P. Joshi also contributed to the excavation of this civilization. Hence, it is clear that V.A. Smith was not associated with the discovery of Harappan Civilization rather was a British Indologist and art historian.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to the report of IIT Kharagpur study group, continuous low rainfall for how many years was the cause of fall of the Indus Valley civilization?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the reports of IIT Kharagpur, the continuous low or negligible rainfall for 900 years was the cause of fall of the Indus Valley Civilization. In other words, it can be said that continuous drought for 900 years led to the fall of Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: When did the use of iron begin in Indian subcontinent?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: The history of early iron smelting, practiced by the tribal artisans in diff erent regions of ancient India dates back to 1300 to 1200 B.C. Most archaeologists accept around 1000 B.C. as start of the iron age in subcontinent. So earliest use of Iron in the Indian subcontinent can be placed around 3000 years ago. Hence option (e) None of the above is correct.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mandala of Rig Veda is completely dedicated to ‘Soma’?
questions.explanation: Rig Veda is the oldest Veda. It comprises of 10 Mandals. The 9th Mandal of Rig Veda comprises 114 hymns dedicated to ‘Soma.’

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Boghaz-Koi is important because:

options.a: It was an important trading centre between Central Asia and Tibet
options.b: Inscriptions were found which mentioned the names of Vedic Gods and Goddesses
options.c: Original Texts of the Vedas were composed here

questions.answer_text: Inscriptions were found which mentioned the names of Vedic Gods and Goddesses
questions.explanation: Boghaz-Koi inscription (Asia Minor, Turkiye) is important because there is mention of four Vedic Gods, namely Indra, Varuna, Mitra, and Nasatya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Famous Battle of ‘Ten Kings’ was fought on the bank of the river:
questions.explanation: There is an ancient story mentioned in the Rig Veda called the Dasharajnya or ‘Battle of 10 Kings’ on the bank of the Parushni River. There lived a descendant of India’s eponymous king Bharata, named Sudas. The greatest achievement of Sudas was his thumping victory over a confederacy of ten kings.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gayatri Mantra is found in which book?
questions.explanation: The Gayatri Mantra was fi rst written in Sanskrit in the Rig Veda by the Brahmarshi Vishwamitra. Its meaning is “May the Almighty God illuminate our intellect to lead us along the righteous path.”

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which phase, the concept of untouchability was put clearly?
questions.explanation: The concept of untouchability assumed a defi nite shape in the early Christian era which was the period known as the era of Dharmashastra in ancient Indian history. During this period, the Brahmanical religion was in ascedence. Various scriptures were being written and the social customs of diff erent types were practised strictly and untouchability was one of them.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which ancient Indian text, composed during the later Vedic period, contains philosophical hymns and discussions on cosmology and ethics?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Upanishads are a collection of philosophical texts composed during the later Vedic period in ancient India. They explore concepts of cosmology, ethics, and the nature of reality. The Upanishads are late Vedic and post-Vedic Sanskrit texts that "document the transition from the archaic ritualism of the Veda into new religious ideas and institutions" and the emergence of the central religious concepts of Hinduism. They are the most recent addition to the Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Hinduism, and deal with meditation, philosophy, consciousness, and ontological knowledge.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where did Mahatma Buddha’s ‘Mahaparinirvana’ take place?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha delivered his fi rst sermon at the site of Deer Park at Sarnath. Later he moved towards Kosala, Kapilavastu, Vaishali and Rajgriha to propagate the teachings of Buddhism. The king of Kosala Prasenjit with his entire family adopted discipleship of Buddha. During his campaign, he reached ‘Pava’, the capital of Mallas. At Pava, Buddha stayed in the mango grove of Chund, the blacksmith. There Chund provided him a large amount of Sukaramaddava, which resulted in sickness with the fl ow of blood and violent deadly pains, but Buddha reached Kushinara or Khushi Nagar (Capital of Republic of Malla). Here he abandoned his body in 483 B.C. at the age of 80 years. It is also known as Mahaparinirvana.

questions.question: The ruler of Suvarnabhumi, who founded a Buddhist monastery at Nalanda and requested Devapala through his ambassador to grant, fi ve villages for its maintenance, was:

options.e: None of the above/More than on of the above.

questions.explanation: Balaputradeva was the ruler of Suvarnabhumi who founded a Buddhist monastery at Nalanda and requested Devapala through his ambassador to grant five villages for its maintenance.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: At which place did Mahatma Buddha give his fi rst ‘Dhammachakkhapavathana’?
questions.explanation: After his enlightenment in Bodh Gaya, Buddha went to Sar-nath, where he delivered his fi rst sermon which is known in Pali as the ‘Dhammachakkhapavathana’ or “Dharma Chakra Pravartana.” Sarnath is one of the four holy places associated with the life of Buddha. Other three important places related to Buddhism are Lumbini (the birthplace of Buddha) Bodh Gaya (the place of enlightenment of Buddha) and Kushi Nagar (place of his death popularly known as Mahaparinir-vana in Buddhism).

questions.explanation: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalvana, Kashmir under the patronage of Kushan King Kanishka and the president of this council was Vasumitra, with Ashvag-hosa as his deputy president. This council distinctly divided Buddhism into two sects, namely Mahayana and Hinayana.

Match Schedule- I and Schedule- II and select correct answer from the codes given below - Schedule - I Schedule - II A. Birth 1. Sarnath B. Enlightenment 2. Bodh Gaya C. First preaching 3. Lumbini D. Death 4. Kushinagar Code : A B C D
questions.explanation: Mahatma Buddha was born in 563 B.C. in Lumbini near Kapilvastu (Nepal). He got enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. Buddha gave his fi rst sermon at Sarnath (Rishipattan) called “Dharma Chakra Pravartana” and died in Kushinagar called “Mahaparinirvana.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In Indian art, the construction of ‘Stupa’, ‘Chaitya’ and ‘Vihara’ is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: 'Stupa', 'Chaitya', and 'Vihara' all are related to Buddhism. Stupa is a dirt burial mound faced with stone. In Buddhism, the earliest stupas contained portions of the Buddha's ashes, and as a result, it began to be associated with the body of the Buddha. Chaitya is a place of worship while Vihara is the dwelling place of monks.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mahabodhi Temple has been built at Bodh Gaya where-

options.c: Gautama Buddha gave his fi rst sermon

questions.explanation: For full six years, Gautam sought a due solution to the suff er-ings, ultimately he got enlightenment at the age of 35 years at Bodh Gaya under the Pipal tree on a Vaisakh Purnima night. Hence he was called “Buddha.” Mahabodhi temple was built at this site.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The ‘Bodhi Vriksh’ in Bodh Gaya belongs to which generation of its family?
questions.explanation: At present, the ‘Bodhi Vriksh’ at the Mahabodhi temple is not the real one, where Mahatma Buddha got enlightenment. According to the Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese traveler, King Shashank destroyed the original tree in the seventh century A.D. The present tree which we see was planted by the orders of Alexander Cunningham and called the fi fth generation tree. It is a heritage site and only fallen leaves of this tree are allowed to touch and pick.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: After the Mahaparinirvana of Lord Buddha, the fi rst Buddhist council was held at:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The fi rst Buddhist council was held just after the death (Ma-haparinirvana) of Lord Buddha during the tenure of Magadh king Ajatashatru in the Sattapanni caves of Rajgriha (Rajgir).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was the fi rst Buddhist Council convened?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The fi rst Buddhist Mahasabha/Sangeet was organised in the Sattapanni cave of Rajagriha immediately after the death of Mahatma Buddha. At that time Ajatashatru was the ruler of Magadha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Tripitakas are the sacred books of the:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tripitaka is the most important holy book of Buddhism. It is divided into three parts - Sutta Pitaka – which consists of sermons and teachings of Buddha, Vinaya Pitaka – a collection of rules governing the Sanghas and Monks and Abhidhamma Pitaka - which deals with the philosophy of Buddhism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where is the highest in the world ‘Vishwa Shanti Stupa’ located in Bihar –
questions.explanation: The Vishwa Shanti Stupa or the World Peace Pagoda (height about 400 metres) situated on the hills of Rajgir in Bihar is the highest Vishwa Shanti Stupa in the world.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies

questions.question: Barabudur is the most wonderful Stupa in the world and its images and sculptures are the fi nest examples of

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Barabudur (Borobudur) Stupa is located on the Island of Java in Indonesia. It sculptures are the fi nest example of Indo-Javanes Art. The construction of this stupa took place in the about 8th and 9th century.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gautam Buddha was elevated to the position of God during the period of:
questions.explanation: The fourth council held during the reign of Kanishka divided Buddhism into two sects, namely Hinayana and Mahayana. In Mahayana, Gautam Buddha was treated as God and they started worshipping Buddha through idols. Hence, Gautam Buddha was elevated to the position of God during the period of Kanishka.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The oldest sculpture of Buddha is made in which style?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: During the Kushana period various statues of Buddha and Bodhisattva (both in standing and sitting position) were made in Mathura and Gandhara style. As per V.S. Agrawal, Buddha statues were fi rst made in Mathura only. As per Huein Tsang fi rst Buddha statue was made in Kaushambi but various other historian gives credit to Gandhara style for the fi rst statue of Buddha. Hence, it cannot be said conclusively where the fi rst statue of Buddha was made.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following state 'Odantipur' Education Centre was situated?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Odantipur (also called Uddandapura) was a prominent educational centre of ancient times. It was situated in Magadha, now Bihar, India. It was established by the Pala emperor Gopala fi rst.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Nalanda University was founded during the dynasty of
questions.explanation: Nalanda was a large Buddhist monastery in the ancient kingdom of Magadha (modern-day Bihar) in India. Historians often described Nalanda as a University. Nalanda fl ourished under the Gupta Empire and was famous for Buddhist religious philosophy.

questions.question: Why was Nalanda University famous in the world?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the founder of Nalanda University?
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was the International University founded in the reign of the Kumar Gupta-I in 450 AD. The great archaeologist Alexander Cunningham identifi ed this site as Nalanda University in 1915-16.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Out of two statements below fi rst is Assertion(A) and second is Reason (R), carefully read both statements. Assertion (A) : Till the end of twelfth century Nalanda Mahavihara lost its glory Reason (R) : State protection ceased to be available to Mahavihara. With respect to the above-mentioned two statements, which of the following is true?

options.a: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.answer_text: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: In ancient India, Nalanda was a famous centre of Buddhist learning and University as well. It was located at Rajgir (at present Rajgriha) in southern Bihar. Nalanda University came into existence during the period of Guptas. By the end of the twelfth century, Mahavihara waned due to Muslim invasion. The importance of Nalanda started declining due to the Pala rulers of Bengal as they started giving protection to Vikramshila University. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Nav Nalanda Mahavihar’ is famous for –
questions.explanation: In 1951, the Nav Nalanda Mahavihar, a modern-day research center for Pali and Buddhism, was founded by the government of Bihar near the ruins of ancient Nalanda.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following is not common between Buddhism and Jainism?
questions.explanation: Avoidance of extremities of penance and enjoyment and choosing a middle path between them was a trait of Buddhism while extreme penance leading to self-mortifi cation was a trait of Jainism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The painting of ‘Bodhisattva Padmapani’ is located at
questions.explanation: The painting of Bodhisattva Padampani is one of the most famous art structure in the cave I of Ajanta. Padampani in Sanskrit literally translates into "one who holds the lotus." The Bodhisattva Padmapani sits among a crowd of devotees, both princesses and commoners with long, dark hair handing down below a jewelled crown, he stands holding his attribute, a blue lotus fl ower in his right hand.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was Mahavira Swami born?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was born in Kundagram (Kundalpur) near Vaishali in 599 B.C. His mother Trishala was the sister of Chetak, the king of Lichchhavi Republic, and his father Siddhartha was the head of Gyatrik Kshatriya. Nandivardhan was his elder brother.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Mahavira Jain breathed his last at –
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was born in Kundagram near Vaishali in 599 B.C. He attained Nirvana at the age of (approx) 72 years in 527 B.C. in Pavapuri, located near Rajgriha (Rajgir).

questions.question: The salvation place of Mahavirji, the originator of Jain religion, is located at -:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Triratna or Three Jewels, i.e., right knowledge, right faith and right action are related to which of the following?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Three means are said to be important for ‘Moksha’ in Jain philosophy: Right faith, Right action (conduct) and Right knowledge. These are known as ‘Triratna’ in Jain religion. Freedom from the bondage and eff ect of evil omens is called Sanvar Tattva to make the spirit free from the bondage of all. The destruction of Karma is the Nirjara element.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is the earliest holy book of Jain?
questions.explanation: The Fourteen Purvas is the ancient Jain scripture, which was preached by all Tirthankaras. At the time of the last Nand Ruler, Sambhootvijay and Bhadrabahu were the presidents of the Sangha. These two were the last to possess knowledge about the ancient Jain texts 14 Purvas given by Mahavira.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The fi rst disciple of Lord Mahavira was –
questions.explanation: Among the early visitors to Mahavira during his wandering was Jamali, his son-in-law. Jamali met Mahavira while the later was in Kshatriya- Kundagram, the village where Mahavira was born. He took the vow together with fi ve hundred of the warrior caste. Jamali was the fi rst disciple of Lord Mahavira.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Ajivaka’, sect was founded by:
questions.explanation: Makkhali Gosala was a disciple of Mahavira in the early period, later fell out with Mahavira due to the diff erence of opinion with him and founded an independent creed “Ajivaka.” The belief of the sect is known as ‘Niyatiwad’ according to which every matter in the world is being controlled and operated by destiny (fate).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who used the caves of Barabar as their shelter-house?
questions.explanation: The act of cutting the mountain caves and developing them as residences was fully developed during the period of Ashoka and his grandson Dasaratha. Residences were made for Ajivaka followers after cutting the hills of Barabar and Nagarjuni.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following kings was strongly inclined towards Jainism?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kharavel, the Chedi dynasty ruler of Kalinga was one of the greatest emperors in ancient India history. An inscription without date has been received from the 'Hathigumpha' of the Udayagiri hill, located three miles from Bhubaneswar in Odisha province. This record is the only source to know the history of Kharavel. It had a heavy inclination towards Jainism. The Hathigumpha inscription is in Prakrit Language.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Gorathagiri in the Barabar Hills was conquered by

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Gorathagiri in the Barabar Hill was conquered by Emperor Kharavela. Kharavela was the greatest king of the Mahameghavahana dynasty of Kalinga, it was an ancient ruling dynasty of Kalinga after the decline of the Mauryan Empire. The primary source for Kharavela is the Hathigumpha inscription Udaygiri.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis made devotional religion popular in
questions.explanation: Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis made Bhakti (devotional) religion popular in Northern India. They criticised the ritual and other aspects of conventional religion and the social order. They also advocated renunciation of the world.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who contributes the most in the development of Bhagavata sect?
questions.explanation: The Bhagavata or Vaishnava religion reached its peak in the reign of Gupta kings. Gupta kings were follower of the Vaishnava religion, and they made it a religion of the state. Most of the Gupta rulers hold the title of ‘Parambhagavata.’ Garuda, the mount (Vahana) of Lord Vishnu was the state symbol of Guptas.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In ancient times, the area to the south of the Ganga was known as

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: In ancient times the area along rivers to the south of Ganga was known as Magadha. Takshashila was situated between the Indus and Jhelum. Chola was situated in the south of Godavari river. Anarta was a Vedic era kingdom of ancient India. Hence option (e) None of the above is correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who founded Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra was founded by Ajatashatru, who was the successor of Bimbisara. He built a fort at the confl uence of the Son and Ganga rivers. Udayin shifted the capital of the Magadha Empire from Rajgriha to Pataliputra. However, the Bihar Public Service Commission has allowed answer option (a).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: By which ruler Pataliputra was chosen as the capital for the fi rst time?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which ruler founded the beautiful city, Pataliputra?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Patliputra was founded by Ajatshatru, who was the successor of Bimbisara. Udayin shifted the capital of Magadha Empire from Rajgriha to Pataliputra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which ruler had made Pataliputra the capital of his empire for the fi rst time?
questions.explanation: Pataliputra was established by Ajatashatru, the ruler of Haryanka dynasty at the confl uence of the Son and Ganga rivers and Udayin transferred his capital from Rajgriha to Pataliputra. But Udayin is not mentioned in the above options. Here, Chandragupta Maurya will be the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to the Mahavamsa, Bimbisara ascended the throne at the age of

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bimbisara was the king of the Magadha Empire in eastern India. Bimbisara was the son of Bhattiya. He ascended to throne at the age of 15. He established the Haryanka dynasty and laid the foundation of Magadha with the fortifi cation of a village, which later became the city of Pataliputra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which century did the fi rst Magadhan Empire rise?
questions.explanation: The fi rst Magadhan empire fl ourished in the 6th century B.C. The actual founder of this empire was King Bimbisara (approximately 544-492 century B.C.). He was related to the Haryanka dynasty.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which was the fi rst capital of ancient Mahajanapada Magadh?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Magadh was an ancient kingdom in southern Bihar. Its fi rst capital was Rajgriha (Modern day Rajgir) which was also known as Girivraj. During the reign of Udayin (Haryanka dynasty), the Capital was moved to Patliputra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one was the capital of Magadh?
questions.explanation: In the given options two options (a) and (c) are correct. The initial capital, of Magadha was Girivraj, later Udayin made Pataliputra the capital, which remained the capital of Magadha till the Gupta period. Diff erent details are found in Buddhist texts and Puranas regarding the fi rst dynasty that ruled the Magadha empire. According to the Puranas. The fi rst king of this dynasty was Jarasandha, who made Girivraj his capital.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Magadha and Anga plains are parts of which of the following?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Magadha and Anga plains are the parts of Middle Ganga Valley.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: By whom the fi rst republic of the world was established in Vaishali –
questions.explanation: The Lichchhavi dynasty of Vaishali established the fi rst republic in the world. Vaishali took its name from King Vishal of the Mahabharata era. Vaishali is a great Buddhist pilgrimage and also the birthplace of Lord Mahavira.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was the world’s fi rst republican system in the sixth century BC?
questions.explanation: The world's fi rst republic system was in Vaishali in the sixth century B.C. In fact, in the 6th century B.C., where there was monarchical governance was prevalent in two states named. Vajji and Malla. Vajji was a confederation of 8 states, in which the lichchhavis of Vaishali were the most powerful.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The list of sixteen Mahajanapadas is available in –
questions.explanation: The 16 Mahajanapadas of 6th century B.C. were mentioned in Buddhist text ‘Anguttara Nikaya’ and Jain text 'Bhagwati Sutra'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which was the capital of Magadha?
questions.explanation: Rajgriha was the first capital of Magadha. Where the fi rst ‘Buddhist Council’ was organized and Lord Mahavir sermoned fi rst). According to Puranas, the fi rst dynasty to rule over Magadh was Brihadrath dynasty. King Brihadrath's son, Jarasandha, made Girivraja (Rajgir) his capital. Later on, Udayin, son of Ajatashatru, moved the capital to Patliputra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which was the initial capital of Magadha?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the name of the dynasty of Ajatshatru?
questions.explanation: Ajatashatru (492-460 BC) belonged to Haryanka dynasty. He became king after killing his father Bimbisara.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the Physician of Magadh ruler Bimbisara?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Jeevaka was the doctor of Bimbsara the ruler of Magadha. Bimbisara also sent him for the treatment of Awanti Naresh Chand Pradyot.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which dynasty did rule over Magadha after Nanda Dynasty?
questions.explanation: Nanda dynasty of Magadha was founded after the end of Shishunaga dynasty. There were 9 kings in Nanda dynasty- (1) Ugrasen, called Mahapadma in Puranas (2) Panduk (3) Pandugati (4) Bhootpal (5) Rastrapal (6) Govishanak (7) Dashasiddhak (8) Kaivart (9) Dhanananda. During last years of Nanda dynasty, people became turbulent because of extortion and imposing heavy taxes on small items. By taking advantage of this, Chandragupta Maurya with the help of Chanakya killed Dhanananda and established Maurya Empire. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the last King of Karnata dynasty?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The last ruler of Karnata Dynasty was Harisimha Dev. He was a great patron of art and literature. He was the pro-founder of Panji system.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following rulers of Magadha was the contemporary of Alexander, the Great?
questions.explanation: There were eight inheritors of Mahapadmananda found in purans and Buddhist texts. Dhanananda was the ruler contemporary of Alexander, the Great Greek writers referred him to as Agrammes.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who wrote the Periplus of the Erythraen Sea?
questions.explanation: Th e ‘Periplus of the Erythaean Sea’ is a Greco-Roman periplus (manuscript document). It describes the opportunities for navigation and trade from the ports of Roman Egypt. It was written by an anonymous sailor from Alexandria. It has also mentioned the items to be imported and exported from India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The fi rst Empire was established by which ruler in India?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya is considered one of the greatest emperors of India. He was the fi rst emperor who brought together the small fragmented kingdoms of the country and combined them into a single large empire. He expanded his empire to the edge of what is now known as Iran. He was the one who fi rst unifi ed India politically.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya fi gures prominently in the book of –
questions.explanation: Mudrarakshasa authored by Vishakhadatta provides various information about the reign of Chandragupta Maurya. Dhundiraja had written a commentary on Mudrarakshasa. In this drama, Chandragupta is described as the son of Nandraja. This book depicts Chandragupta as "Vrishal" and "Kulheen".

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandra Gupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: William Jones was the first scholar who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandra gupta Maurya. Aerian and Plutarch also described him as Androkottos.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Kautilya's Arthashastra is a book on -

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Arthashastra by Kautilya is the treatise on polity during the Mauryan monarch/kingdom. The Saptang theory of the state was fi rst introduced in it, which includes the seven elements of the states, these are – The King (Swami), Minister (Amatya), Territory (Janpada), Fort (Durg), Treasury (Kosa), Army (Danda) and Allies (Mitra). Arthashastra gives a detailed description of the then administration and agrarian system.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Kautilya’s Arthashastra deals with the aspects of –
questions.explanation: Arthashastra renders a wide range of information about Mauryan dynasty. This is the unique saga of political policies.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Chandragupta’s palace situated at Pataliputra is mainly made up of –
questions.explanation: The archaeological remains of the Mauryan period have been discovered in Bulandibagh and Kumrahar near Patna (Ancient Pataliputra). It is known that the palace of Chandragupta Maurya was made of wood. The excavation was carried out by D.B. Spooner. The remains of the city wall from Bulandibagh and the remains of palace from Kumhrar have been found during the excavation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who amongst the following Mauryan rulers did conquer the Deccan?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Mauryan dynasty, Chandragupta Maurya conquered the Deccan plateau. Jain and Tamil sources inscriptions found at various sites of southern India proved that Chandragupta Maurya expanded his empire into Deccan trap. Inscriptions of Ashoka were also found in many sites in the southern part of India, but he conquered the Kalinga only. In this situation, Chandragupta should be given the credit for Deccan Victory as Victory of Bindusara is doubtful and history never remembered him as a victor.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which book describes Bindusara as an anointed Kshatriya?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Buddhist account Divyavadana describes Bindusara, son of Chandragupta, as an anointed Kshatriya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Inscription which proves Chandragupta’s sway over western India is:
questions.explanation: The description of the construction of irrigation dam by Mauryan provincial governor “Pushyagupta” was found from the Junagarh rock inscription of Rudradaman which proves that this western part of India was once the part of Mauryan empire.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one territory of the following was not a part of Ashoka’s empire?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka was not part of Ashoka’s territory. The second inscription of Ashoka clarifies that Chola, Pandayas, Sattiyaputta, Keralaputta and Tamraparni (Sri Lanka) were not the part of Mauryan reign. That's why they were called as edge states.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: A Buddhist Council during the reign of Ashoka was held at –
questions.explanation: According to Sinhalese Folklore –“Dipavamsa” and “Mahavamsa”, the Third Buddhist Council was held in “Pataliputra” during the reign of Ashoka.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Language used in the inscriptions of Ashoka is:
questions.explanation: Ashokan inscriptions describe the history of Ashoka properly. The inscription can be divided into three classes; (1) Rock inscription / petrography (2) Column inscription (3) Cave inscription. Rock inscription is the group of 14 various inscriptions that found at eight diff erent places – Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra, Kalsi, Girnar, Dhauli, Jaugada, Yerraguddi and Sopara. Most of the inscription of Ashoka are written in Prakrit language and Brahmi script, only two inscriptions, Shahbajgarhi and Mansehra’s are in Kharoshti script. One ruined inscription, written in Aramaic script, was found in Taxila. Shar-i-Kuna (Kandhar Inscription) is in the bilingual (Greek-Aramaic) script while one Aramaic script of Ashokan inscription was obtained from Laghman.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following scripts of ancient India was written from right to left?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Kharosthi Script is an ancient script used by the ancient Gandhara culture of South Asia primarily in modern-day Afghanistan & Pakistan Kharoshti was A cursive script written from right to left.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who fi rst deciphered the Brahmi script ?
questions.explanation: The Brahmi script was fi rst deciphered through the letters inscribed on stone tablets. Sir James Prinsep was the fi rst philologist who accomplished the task of deciphering the script of Ashokan inscription. So, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The name by which Ashoka is referred to his inscriptions is :

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The name by which Ashoka is referred in his inscription is "Priyadarshi", "Devanampiya Piyadasi" which means "Beloved of the Gods". He has also been stated as "Ashok Vardhan" in Puranas.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The only pillar on which Ashoka declares himself as the emperor of Magadha –
questions.explanation: Bhabru's (Bairat) inscription proves Ashoka as Buddhist. In the same inscription, he referred to himself as ‘Piyadasi Raja’ Magadha, i.e. the king of Magadha.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The central point in Ashoka's Dhamma is -

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Ashoka's Dhamma was primarily based on policy of peace, non-violence & religious toleration. In his 12th rock edict, religious longanimity and growth of the essence of all communities are mentioned. Hence as per the options, (e) is correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which inscription, Kalinga victory is mentioned?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Kalinga Victory is mentioned in Ashoka's Rock Edict Number 13. Hence, option (e) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Megasthenes was the ambassador of -

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Megasthenes was a Greek historian who came to India in the Fourth Century B.C. as a representative of Seleucus Nicator.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In how many categories did Megasthenes divide the Indian Society?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes divided Mauryan society into seven categories in his book 'Indica', which are as follows : (1) Philosophers (2) Farmers (3) Herdsmen (4) Artisans (5) Military (Soldier) (6) Overseers or Spies (7) Councillors and Assessors. Megasthenese does not mention slavery in India. According to him, no one could marry outside his caste, and no one could take to occupation from the one fi xed for his caste according to the Varnasystem.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The division of Mauryan society into seven classes is particularly mentioned in:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The description of the administration of Pataliputra is available in?
questions.explanation: The description of the administration of Pataliputra is found in Megasthenes' 'Indica'. Megasthenes mentioned six committees of fi ve members each to look after the administration of Pataliputra. He referred to the town offi cials as ‘Astynomi.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the name of Megasthenes’ book?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the author of ‘Indica’?
questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The most famous centre of learning during Mauryan period was:
questions.explanation: At present, Vaishali is a district of Bihar. It was related to both Buddhism and Jainism in ancient times. It was established in 6th century B.C. before the birth of Gautam Buddha (563 B.C.). Mahavira Swami was born in Kundupur near Vaishali. Nalanda – Nalanda was an important centre of Buddhist education. Firstly, Buddha temples were established here in the Gupta period. Taxila – Taxila was a major centre of learning for Hindus and Buddhists who came here from all over the world to get education. It was situated few miles west of present Islamabad. It was most famous during the Mauryan period. Ujjain was the conventional capital of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The last Mauryan emperor was:
questions.explanation: The last Mauryan emperor was Brihadratha. Brihadratha was assassinated by his commander/lieutenant Pushyamitra Shunga in 184 B.C. Pushyamitra Shunga established a new dynasty which is known as Shunga Dynasty.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The decline of the Mauryan Empire was largely due to the economic consequences of Ashoka's policy. Who believed in this fact?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Renowned historian Romila Thapas believes that it was the economic consequences of Ashoka's policies that led to the decline of the Mauryan Empire.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Pradyota was the king of–

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Pradyota was the ruler of the ancient Mahajanapada Avanti. Avanti is located in the present-day Madhya Pradesh State. Pradyota was contemporary to Gautama Buddha and Bimbisara.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which inscription tells about the various achievements of Rudradaman-I?
questions.explanation: The Junagadh inscription written in Sanskrit dated approx. 150 A.D. credits Rudradaman-I for supporting the cultural arts and Sanskrit literature and reconstructing the dam built by the Mauryas. In fact, he repaired the embankments of the lake Sudarshana, which was constructed by the Mauryas or checking fl oods.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to the rock inscription in Sanskrit, composed around second century CE, Sudarshan Lake, an artifi cial reservoir, was repaired by

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Junagadh inscription written in Sanskrit, composed around second century CE credits Rudradaman-I for repairment of Sudarshan Lake which was an artifi cial reservoir constructed by Mauryas.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following fi rst issued gold coins on a large scale?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kushan emperor Vima Kadphises, who was the father of Kanishka-I, had introduced gold coins on a large scale in India. He is known as the First King, who introduced gold coins, while Kujul Kadphises circulated copper coins.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which dynasty ruled over India after Shunga dynasty?
questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Shunga emperors was Devabhuti. He was killed by his minister (Vasudeva Kanva). The Shunga dynasty was then replaced by the subsequent Kanvas. They were also Brahmin like Shunga.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the leader of the Ghadar Movement, a revolutionary movement aimed at overthrowing British rule in India?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Kartar Singh Sarabha (24 May 1896 — 16 November 1915) was an Indian revolutionary. He was 15-years old when he became a member of the Ghadar Party; he then became a leading luminary member and started fi ghting for the independence movement. He was one of the most active members of the movement.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Art of Gandhara style fl ourished during the reign of –
questions.explanation: The Gandhara School of Art was developed during the Kushan period. It was based on Gandhara style. They were provided adequate encouragement and protection from Kanishka. Gandhara art was infl uenced by Greek art.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: King Kharavela is related to –
questions.explanation: Kharavela of Chedi dynasty was the king of Kalinga present day Odisha, India. Much of the available information about Kharavela comes from the undated and partially damaged Hathigumpha inscription, plus a few other minor inscriptions found in Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves, in present-day Odisha. This is the only known source of Kharavela inscriptions. The Kharavela is believed to be a follower of Jainism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following kings had heavily leaned towards Jainism?
questions.explanation: Kharavela of Chedi dynasty was the king of Kalinga, present in Odisha, India. Much of the available information about Kharavela comes from the Hathigumpha inscription. He is believed to be a follower of Jainism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Kaling king Kharavel was related to-

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/ More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The founder of the Chedi dynasty of Kalinga was a person named Mahameghavahana. Therefore the name of this dynasty also became the Mahameghavahana dynasty. The most powerful ruler of this dynasty was Kharavela. The Hathigumpha inscription is the only means of studying Kharavela's history.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Gupta ruler assumed the throne after killing his elder brother?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: After Samudragupta, his son Ramagupta become the ruler, but He was not able to oppose the invasion of Shaka, his brother Chandragapupta II Killed Ramagupta and married his wife Dhruv Devi and won against Shaka.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is called ‘the Napoleon of Ancient India’?
questions.explanation: Historian V.A. Smith in his composition 'The Early History of India’ called Samudragupta (335-375 A.D.) of Gupta dynasty as ‘Napoleon of India’ for his great military conquests.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to Chinese source, Meghavarman, the ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a missionary to which of the following Gupta Kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
questions.explanation: Meghavarman sent a missionary to Samudragupta to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya. Samudragupta granted permission to Buddhist king of Ceylon (Sri Lanka) Meghavarman to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Gupta emperor who defeated the ‘Hunas’ was:
questions.explanation: The fi rst invasion of Hunas took place during the reign of Skandagupta and Hunas were comprehensively defeated by him. This invasion was just like a raid, and there was not lasting impact on India, but this invasion intensifi ed the decline of the Gupta Empire. Hunas annexed many regions of the north-west in the transition period of the 5th-6th centuries after the death of Skandagupta.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following ports was in use for the north Indian trade during the Gupta period?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: During the Gupta period Tamralipti of Bengal was an important port that used for trading with South-East Asia, China, Sri Lanka, Java, Sumatra etc. Bhrigukatchha (Bharuch) was on important port of western India from where trade of North India with western countries occurred through sea-route. During the Gupta period, most of the Indian trade happened with South-East Asia, hence Tamralipti was most important port of this period. However, Bharuch, Kalyan, Cambay etc. were also used for North Indian trade. Hence most suitable answer would be more than one which is option (e).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Gupta ruler is mentioned as 'Param Bhagawata' in Nalanda Copper Plates?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Copper plate inscription of Samudragupta from Nalanda and Gaya describes Param Bhagavata title of Samudragupta.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In pre-Gupta times, a large number of lead coins were issued by the

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Satavahanas were the early rulers of the region between the rivers, Godavari and the Krishna. They were also referred to as the Andhras. They soon brought under their control, both the Western-Deccan and Central India. Their coins were pre-dominatly of copper and lead, however, silver issues are also known. These coins carried the motifs of fauna like elephants, lions, bulls, horses etc. after juxtaposed against motifs from nature like hills, trees etc. The silver coins of the Satavahanas carried protraits and bilingual legends which were inspired by the Kshatrapa type.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following is known for his work on medicine during the Gupta period?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sushruta is called the father of surgery. He was a resident of Kashi. It is believed that his period was around 600 B.C. Shaunak was the sage of the Rigveda. Shudraka was a dramatist of the Gupta period (litterateur). Saumilla is a playwright of Gupta period who has been remembered by Kalidasa with Bhasa and Kaviputra. Thus, none of the above had worked in the fi eld of medicine during the Gupta period. Although Bihar Public Service Commission in its initial answer sheet has considered the correct answer as option (a). Since the Gupta period begins with 275-A.D. (Sri Gupta), which is about 875 years later than the valid period of Sushruta (usually 600 BC), it is not reasonable to consider Sushruta a contemporary of the Gupta period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The gradual decline of towns was an important feature of which period?
questions.explanation: During the Gupta period, towns declined gradually. All the towns which were prosperous in the valley, most of them had declined in that age. A major city, Patliputra became village when Hiuen-Tsang came to India. Mathura, Sonpur, and Sohgama- all major cities provided evidence of a decline in this age. So, we can say that the gradual decline of towns is an important feature of the Gupta period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which ruling dynasty donated maximum villages to temples and Brahmins?
questions.explanation: The ruler of Gupta dynasty donated a maximum number of villages to temples and Brahmins. Also, the income generated from the land of the village used to be given to the owner of the land.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the land revenue rate in Gupta age?
questions.explanation: A person who used to cultivate on the offi cial land of the ruler had to pay a part of crop-products as tax in Gupta period which was the sixth portion of the production. Land revenue is known as ‘Udrang’ and “Bhag” in Gupta inscriptions.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the land revenue rate in religious books?
questions.explanation: In every religious text, the land revenue rate is 1/6th of the produce.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which type of land was called 'Aprahat'?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Uncultivable lands were called 'Aprahat'. It was a term of the revenue system in the Gupta period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Chinese traveller 'Sungyun' was came to India in:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Chinese traveller 'Sungyun' came to India in about 518 to 521 A.D. He collected texts of Buddha's preaching in his three years of travel.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The account of the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta is known as

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan and Berber explorer. He is known for his extensive travels, accounts of which were published in the Rihla. Rihla was a travel book written by Ibn Battuta in Arabic. He came to India during the regime of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following philosophies of India propounded the atom theory?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Maharishi Kanada is associated with atom theory. He was a scientist & philosopher who founded Vaisheshika School of Indian Philosophy in which he gave the atomistic approach to physics and philosophy in Sanskrit.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who has written the ‘Harshacharita’?
questions.explanation: Eminent author Banabhatta composed the text "Harshacharita". This is the major source of Pushyabhuti dynasty. It is a fable in which the author presents the description of his contemporary ruler and biographies of their ancestors.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who laid the foundation of Vardhana Dynasty?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to Banbhatt's composition 'Harshcharita' the establishment of Vardhan Dynasty was done by a person named Pushyabhuti, in Thaneshwar/Sthaneswar. Harshvardhan was the greatest ruler of this dynasty.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Poet Bana was inhabitant of –
questions.explanation: Banabhatta, the poet, was born in the village Prithikuta, on the bank of Son River in Aurangabad district (Present Bihar). The names of his father and mother were Chitrabhanu and Rajdevi respectively.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Chinese traveller visited India during Harshavardhana’s rules?
questions.explanation: The arrival of Hiuen-Tsang was the most important event of Harsha’s period. He desired to visit the places related to Mahatma Buddha and study Buddhist texts, which were available in India. He departed for India in 629 A.D. from Changan, the capital of Tang Ruler. He wrote a book on his tour to India named ‘Sei-Yu-Kei.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of Chandragupta-II.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements : 1. Fa-Hien was a Chinese pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Harsha. 2. Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II while Hiuen-Tsang visited the court of Harshvardhana. Hence neither statement is correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: During Hiuen-Tsang tour in India most famous city for the production of cotton clothes was:
questions.explanation: The traveller of China Hiuen-Tsang arrived in India during Harsha’s period and stayed here. According to Hiuen-Tsang, Mathura was famous for the production of cotton textiles. He also mentioned that the reason for the prosperity of Thanesar was its trade. Ujjayini as well as Kannauj were economically prosperous too.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang studied at the University of –
questions.explanation: The traveller from China, Hiuen Tsang arrived in India during Harsha’s period and went to Nalanda University in 637 A.D. Acharya Sheelbhadra was the Vice-Chancellor of Nalanda University at that time. He learned Yogashashtra there for almost one and a half year. He also delivered a speech during his second visit to Nalanda University.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Chinese traveller I-tsing was on the tour of Bihar in about:
questions.explanation: With his desire to see the relics of Buddhism, Chinese traveller I-tsing (671-695 A.D.) with his 37 Buddhist associates decided to travel to Western countries. Later his associate left him, and he alone moved to India from Canton city. He came to India through western sea route and returned to China via Sumatra.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Nalanda University was destroyed by –
questions.explanation: Nalanda University attracted scholars and students from Tibet, China, Greece and Persia. It was ransacked and destroyed by the army of Bakhtiyar Khalji at the end of the twelfth century. It can be seen as the coup de grace (fi nal blow) to the decline of Buddhism in India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Nalanda Vihar was destroyed by :

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bakhtiyar Khalji captured entire Bihar between 1193 A.D. to 1203 A.D. He destroyed Nalanda and Vikramshia Vihar. Later control was also established over some parts of Bengal and Assam. Thus he was the real founder of Turkish power in Bihar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: How many rulers of Aryavarta have been mentioned in 21st line of Allahabad Pillar Inscription?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Allahabad Pillar Inscription or the Prayaga Prashasti mentions Samudragupta conquering Nine kings during his second campaign of Aryavarta.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who has argued that the Gupta and post-Gupta periods saw a decline in the money economy?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: R.S. Sharma has argued that the Gupta and Post-Gupta period saw a decline in money economy. He points out that the Guptas issued many gold coins, but comparatively few silver and copper coins.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the ruler of India during the 7th century CE known for his patronage of Buddhism and support for cultural activities?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Harsha, also known as Harshavardhana, was a notable Indian Emperor who ruled a signifi cant portion of North India during the 7th century CE. Harsha was a devout Buddhist, and his military campaigns often incorporated a commitment to the spread and support of Buddhism.Despite his own faith, he practiced religious tolerance and was known for his benevolence towards other religious communities, including Hindus, Jains, and Buddhists.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The associates of Khajuraho Temple Architecture were –
questions.explanation: Khajuraho temple evidences the excellence of Chandela architecture. These temples are located in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh. They were built between 10th–12th century. Kandariya Mahadev temple is the best among these temples.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The attractive doors of the temples of South India are called-

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The attractive gate of the temples of the south is called 'Gopuram'. The Dravidian style fl ourished during the rule of Pandyas and Cholas. In the Pandya period, the temples were small, but many ramparts were built around their courtyard. Their gateways, which were called 'Gopurams', were grand, spacious and richly ornamented with craftsmanship. The specialty of the Chola period architecture is not the temple, but the Gopuram.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)
questions.question: Who established trade relations with Roman empire?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: India's trade with the Roman Empire started with the Chera Kingdom during the Sangam period. Many Roman things were found in Arikamedu (Puducherry).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)
questions.question: Which medieval Indian empire was famous for elaborated local self-government?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A special feature of the Chola dynasty was the autonomy of village administration which was a speciality of them. The Chola village administration was very systematic and well-developed. In fact, the autonomous administration was implemented in the village only during the Chola era.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)
questions.question: The Chola age was most famous for:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)
questions.question: Who was the founder of Chola dynasty?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Chola Empire was founded by Vijayalaya, who was initially a feudatory chieftain of the Pallavas. He captured Tanjavur in 850 A.D. The Shiv temple of Tanjavur, Rajarajeswara or Brihadeeswara temple was built during the time of Rajaraja I.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)
questions.question: Which of the following dynasties is not mentioned in Sangam literature?
questions.explanation: The origin and elevation of Chola, Cheras and Pandyas are mentioned in Sangam Literature. Kadamb or any other dynasty is not mentioned in Sangam literature.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)
questions.question: Why was ‘Uraiyur’ famous in Sangam Era?

options.a: An important trade centre of spices
options.b: An important trade centre of cotton
options.c: An important centre of foreign trade
options.d: An important centre of domestic trade

questions.answer_text: An important trade centre of cotton
questions.explanation: Uraiyur was a very signifi cant town during Sangam Era, located on the bank of Cauvery River in Tiruchirappalli (Tamil Nadu). It was known as Koli and Varanam and was the major centre of cotton. It is mentioned in “Periplus of the Erythraen Sea.”

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following was the writer of Mudrarakshasa?
questions.explanation: Mudrarakshasa written by Vishakhadatta is a drama in Sanskrit. Although written during the Gupta period, it describes how Chandragupta with the assistance of Kautilya overthrew the Nandas. It also gives a picture of the socio-economic condition under the Mauryas.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Kumarasambhava,’ an epic poem was composed by –
questions.explanation: The famous books of Kalidasa: - Abhigyanshakuntalam, Kumarsambhavam, Malavikagnimitram, Meghadutam etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is the name of Kalhana’s book?
questions.explanation: Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Name the source that is silent about the trade routes of ancient India:
questions.explanation: Sangam Sahitya is silent about the trade routes of ancient India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The author of ‘Swapnavasavadatta’ is
questions.explanation: 'Swapnavasavadattam' is a Sanskrit play written by great poet Bhasa.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Indian Philosophy has given the theory of atom?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to Vaisheshika philosophy, the universe is created from Atoms. Maharshi Kanad was the originator of this philosophy.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who wrote the book “Kiratarjuniya”?
questions.explanation: The author of the book 'Kiratarjuniya' is Bharavi. The story of this book is taken from the Mahabharata. It describes the battle between Arjuna and Shiva in form of "Kirat".

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The author of ‘Prithviraj Raso’ is –
questions.explanation: Prithviraj Raso describes the battles of Prithviraj Chauhan. It was written by Chand Bardai.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Epigraphic records (Inscriptions) suggest that in ancient India, the rulers of Bihar had contact with –
