questions.explanation: The Pala king Devpala was Buddhist. He donated fi ve villages at the request of Java king Balputradeva of Sailendra Dynasty for developing a Buddhist Vihar in Nalanda.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Vikramshila University in Bihar : 1. It was located in the present-day Banka district of Bihar. 2. It was established by King Gopala I of the Pala dynasty. 3. The ‘Vajrayana’ sect of Buddhism fl ourished here. 4. Other subjects like Astronomy, Logic, Law, Grammar and Philosophy were also taught here. Which of the above statements are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Vikramshila University is located in Bhagalpur and not in the Banka district. It was established by Dharmapala of Pal dynasty and not by Gopala I. Hence Statement 1 and 2 are incorrect. Rest are correct.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which ruler of Bengal founded the ancient University called ‘Vikramshila.’
questions.explanation: King Dharmapala 770-810 A.D. of Pala dynasty established the Vikramshila University. After the downfall of Nalanda University. Vikramshila University was developed as the main centre for the Buddhist religion.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Vikramshila University was established by

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Huna King Toramana was defeated by the Aulikara King

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Toramana was a Huna king who ruled in northern India. Sanjeli inscription of Toramana speaks of his conquest and control over Malwa and Gujarat. His territory also included Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Kashmir. According to the Risthal inscription, discovered in 1983, Huna king Toramana was defeated by Aulikara king Prakashadharma of Malwa.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Muhammad Ghori granted fi rst Iqta in India to –
questions.explanation: Soon after the victories of Ghori, Iqta system was established in North India. In 1192 A.D., Muhammad Sam of Ghori (Muhammad Ghori) appointed Qutb-ud-Din-Aibak (Qutbuddin Aibak), as in charge of his Indian territories. He played an important role in the second battle of Tarain. Pleased with his works, Ghori appointed him the administrator of Kuhram and Samana. He had taken care of the administration of North Indian territories conquered by them as representative of Ghori till 1206. During this period, Aibak also expanded Turkish power in northern India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the fi rst ruler of the Slave Dynasty?
questions.explanation: The first ruler of the Slave Dynasty (or named Gulam Dynasty) was Qutb-ud-Din Aibak who ruled from 1206 to 1210 A.D. He established his capital at Lahore. Though he was ugly in appearance, he was intelligent and impressive in behaviour. He was taken as a prisoner and sold to the Qazi of Nishapur named Fakhruddin as a slave in his childhood. He was taken care and pro vided with proper education and military training by the kind-hearted Qazi but soon after the death of the Qazi, his sons sold Aibak to Muhammad Ghori. He was well versed in Islamic theology, horse riding and swordsmanship. Owing to his skill and qualities, he soon attracted the attention of his master and was appointed commander of a troop. Shortly afterwards battles; he was promoted to the post of Amir-i- Akhur, the master of the royal stable. When Ghori invaded India, Aibak came with his master and provided him his active support during battles. The successes of his master by and large depended on his military skill. Ghori was immensely pleased with him, and he appointed him his governor of the Indian empire. In 1206 A.D., on his way to Ghazni, Ghori died. His empire was inherited by his slaves, as he had no son to succeed him. Aibak, who was a viceroy of his Indian Empire was invited by the Amirs of Lahore to assume the powers. He bestowed the title of Malik and Sipahsalar on himself. Muhammad Ghori had no male successor to inherit his empire; hence his nephew, Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascended the throne of Ghori after his death in 1206 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: "His theory of kingship was based on the principles of prestige, power and justice." Who said these words about Balban?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Zia-ud-din Barani said about Balban "His theory of kingship was based on the principles of prestige, power and justice." It is noteworthy that Balban was a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate during the Mamluk dynasty (also known as the slave dyansty). He adopted the policy of 'blood and Iron'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Sultan of Delhi Sultanate was known as 'Lakh Baksh'?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sultan Qutub-ud-din Aibak was the fi rst Muslim ruler of India who ruled from his capital in Lahore. He was known as Lal Baksh because of his generosity.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Muslim ruler whose empire was regarded as a part of Dar-ul-Islam was

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: During the period of Iltutmish, in 1229 A.D. the caliph of Baghdad gave Khillat to Iltulmish. Now the Sultanate was theoretically part of Dar-ul-Islam subject to the caliph of Baghdad.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What is ‘Adhai Din ka Jhonpra’?
questions.explanation: Sultan Qutb-ud-Din Aibak also called “Lakh Baksh” was the fi rst Muslim ruler of India who ruled from his capital in Lahore. He patronized scholars such as Hasan Nizami and Fakhra-i-Mudabbir, both of whom dedicated their works to Aibak. Aibak was the fi rst Muslim ruler who settled in India and ruled unlike the earlier Muslims, who came and only raided and plundered. Though his tenure as a ruler was only four years, and most of them were spent in dealing with the revolts of nobles like Taj-ud-Din Ildiz, Nasir-ud-Din Qubachah and a few Hindu chiefs, he established a fi rm administrative system. He started the construction of Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque at Delhi and Adhai Din ka Jhonpda (Ajmer). He also laid the foundation of the Qutb Minar, which was completed by his successor Iltutmish. He was known as Lakh Baksh for his generosity. He never took the title of "Sultan". but according to the question option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The capital of Qutbuddin Aibak was:
questions.explanation: After the death of Muhammad Ghori in 1206, his General Qutbuddin Aibak, who was in charge of Lahore and north-Indian possessions was invited by Amirs of Lahore to assume the powers of Ghori. The capital of Qutbuddin Aibak was Lahore. Taj-ud-Din Yilduz, Governor of Kirman ascended the throne of Ghazni. It seems that Muhammad Ghori desired that Qutbuddin Aibak should succeed him in India. In his brief reign of four years (1206-10 A.D.), he moved his capital to Lahore to frustrate Yilduz’s ambition of annexing Punjab. He strengthened his position by matrimonial alliances with infl uential rival Turkish Chief. Nasiruddin Qabacha of Multan refused to accept Qutbuddin as the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Due to this, Aibak always stayed in Lahore and never got the chance to move to Delhi.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Qutub Minar was completed by-

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Qutub Minar was completed by the famous ruler Iltutmish.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Iltutmish appointed his fi rst Subedar in Bihar to :
questions.explanation: In 1225 A.D., Iltutmish defeated Hisamuddin Awaz in mountains of Rajmahal near Teliyagarhi and annexed Bihar Shareef and Barh. Awaz had accepted the subordination of Iltutmish. Iltutmish had appointed Malik-Jani as the new Subedar of Bihar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the first Muslim ruler to formulate the 'Theory of Kingship' similar to the 'theory of divine right of the kings'?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Balban was the fi rst ruler to propound the 'theory of King-ship' similar to the 'theory of divine right of the kings. He said, "Sultan is representative of God on earth and his place comes after Paigambar".

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Sultan of Delhi introduced the practice of Sijda?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Balban made some rules and regulations for his court and strictly enforced them. He introduced the rituals of Sizdah (greeting lying on the ground) and Paibos (kissing the feet of the king).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Delhi Sultan is known for adopting the 'blood and iron' policy?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Balban was the first ruler to propound the 'Theory of Kingship' similar to the theory of divine right of the kings. He said, "Sultan is representative of God on earth and his place comes after Paigambar". It is said that he adopted the policy of 'Blood and Iron'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following introduced the Persian festival Nowruz in India?
questions.explanation: Balban introduced the rituals of Sizdah (greeting lying on the ground) and Paibos (Kissing the feet of the king) in his court. He also introduced the rituals to celebrate the Persian festival Nowruz.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the fi rst Muslim conqueror of Bihar?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ikhtiyaruddin Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji, a simple slave of Muhammad Ghori, conquered Bihar between 1193 A.D. to 1203 A.D. and captured the capital Odantapuri after destroying Nalanda and Vikramshila Vihara. He invaded Bengal around 1202-03 A.D. At that time the ruler there was Lakshmansen. He escaped without fighting. The Turkish army entered the capital Nadia and looted badly. The city surrendered in the absence of the king. Lakshmansen fl ed and took refuge in South Bengal and continued to rule there for some time. Famous Persian historian Minhajuddin Siraj in his book Tabaqat-i-Nasiri has described in detail about his attacks in Bihar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following opposed the power of the Khalifa?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Alternatively none of the Sultans opposed the power of the caliph. Iltulmish had obtained recognition from the Khalifa, but Sultan Ghiyasuddin of Bengal had also obtained recognition from the Khalifa. By attacking him, Iltutmish had in a way opposed the power of the Khalifa. Alauddin Khalji, Balban, and Muhahmad Bin Tughlaq were practically independent rulers but none opposed the power of authority of the caliph. There was only Mubarak Khalji who himself took the title of Khalifatullah thus, he opposed the authority of the caliph.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Tughril Khan raised a standard of revolt during whose reign?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tughril Khan revolted during the time of Balban. This rebellion took place in protest against the appointment of Aamir Khan in Bengal. Over time the Tughril fl ed to fearing Balban's Bengal Campaign.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was deputed for the conquest of Dvarasamudra by Ala-ud-din Khalji ?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Malik Kafur was deputed for the conquest of Dvarasamudra by Ala-ud-din Khalji. In 1311 AD, Malik Kafur besieged the Hoy sala capital Dvarasamudra and the defending ruler Veera Ballala III surrendered without much resistance. Ballala agreed to pay the Delhi Sultanate an annual tribute, and surrendered a great amount of wealth, elephants and horses.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: “When he attained Kingship, he was fully independent of from rules and orders of Shariat.” For which Sultan Barani made this statement?
questions.explanation: Ziyauddin Barani made the above statement regarding Alauddin Khalji. Alauddin Khalji was the first king of Delhi, who established the control of the state over religion. In this context, he said explaining his policy “I don’t know what is correct or incorrect by law? I only give a command which I understand suitable for the welfare of the state or special occasion, I don’t know what will happen on the fi nal day of justice.” Alauddin had made alive the thought of Balban. He used to believe in the universality of the king who is only a representative of God on earth. He did not use to take the permission of Khalifa to expand his powers. That’s why he never made a solicitation in front of Khalifa for recognition of his position. He called himself “Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasiri Amir-ul-Mumnin.” Alauddin freed himself from the control of Ulemas.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: "Thus to Ala-ud-din belongs the credit of being the fi rst Turkish Sultan of Delhi to bring the church under the control of the state and to usher in factors that might make the state secular in theory." Who wrote these words?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A.L. Srivastava writes about Ala-ud-din Khilji that "Ala-ud-din was the fi rst Turkish Sultan of Delhi to bring that church under the control of the state and to usher in factor that might make that stak secular in theory."

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who reduced the Khuts and Muqaddams to such an extent that their wives served in the houses of Muslims?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Allauddin Khalji took the authority of tax collection from traditional tax offi cers (Khutt, Mukaddam and Chaudhary). All their privileges were abolished and taxes were collected from them ruthlessly. Thus in the language of Barani, they were reduced to the lowest of low in village society and their women were forced to work in the houses of Muslims for wages.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among army-commanders of Alauddin Khalji died fi ghting against Mongols?
questions.explanation: Zafar Khan, the famous army commander of Alauddin Khalji, died while fi ghting against the Mongols. He was an excellent and courageous commander of his time. Mongols were so impressed by the bravery of Zafar Khan and the persistence of Khalji's army that they backed down by 30 miles. The original name of Zafar Khan was Mian Yusuf Hizbaruddin.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Padmini is associated with Ala-ud-Din’s conquest of Chittor. She was the wife of
questions.explanation: The story of Padmini is well depicted in ‘Padmavat’ written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi in 1540 A.D. According to this, Padmini was the wife of King Ratan Singh. Amir Khusrau mentioned the love story of Suleman and Queen Shaiba in his text and compared Alauddin with Suleman and Padmini with Shaiba. Probably presuming this, Malik Muhammad Jayasi composed Padmavat and the story of Rana Ratan Singh and Queen Padmavati.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the ruler of Devagiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion?
questions.explanation: Ramchandra Dev was the ruler of Devagiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion. In 1296 A.D., the king of Devagiri, Ramchandra Dev after the successful invasion of Alauddin Khalji promised to send the revenue from Ellichpur every year, but during 1305-1306 AD, he did not send the tax to Delhi. Consequently, Alauddin sent an army under the leadership of Malik Kafur to attack Devagiri in 1307 A.D. King Ramchandra Dev was defeated and surrendered. Malik Kafur looted Devagiri and took Ramchandra Dev including his relatives to Delhi. Alauddin behaved with dignity with Ramchandra Dev and gave him the title of ‘Rai Rayan’ and sent him back to his state off ering 1 lakh golden ‘Tankas’ and ‘Navsari’ district. Malik Kafur had also led a campaign against Shankar Dev, the son of Ramchandra in 1312 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: During the regime of which Sultan was the Khalisa land developed on a large scale?
questions.explanation: The main purpose of Alauddin behind the system of revenue and taxes system was to establish a powerful and autocratic state. He snatched all the lands from all those people who got the land as ‘Milq’ (Property given by the state, as prizes, Indarat, pension) and Waqf (land received in charity). Therefore, Khalisa land developed on a large scale.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who started Public Distribution System in Sultanate period?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The ‘Public Distribution System’ was introduced by Ala-ud-din Khalji during Sultanate period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following Sultans provided employment to the unemployed?
questions.explanation: Firuz Shah Tughluq started some welfare programs for common people. He tried to solve the problem of unemployment by opening an office for appointment (employment offi ce) and also appointed many qualifi ed people by their qualifi cations and merits.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Sultan had most numbers of slaves in his court?
questions.explanation: Firuz Shah Tughluq was fond of slaves. The number of his slaves reached up to one lakh eighty thousand. He established a separate department (Diwan-e-Bandgan) to take care of them. He kept his full attention about their education. Each slave was paid 10 to 100 Tankas and sometimes, they also got states. This hobby of Firuz proved detrimental to the state.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Delhi Sultan built the maximum number of canals?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The reign of Firuz Shah Tughluq is famous for building the biggest network of canals for irrigation purposes. They were:- (1) Sutlej to Ghaggar (96 miles) (2) Yamuna to Hisar (150 miles), (3) Sirmor to Hansi, (4) Ghaggar to Firuzabad and (5) Yamuna to Firuzabad.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi introduced measures for improving the quality of fruits?
questions.explanation: Due to his interest in horticulture, Firuz planted 1200 new orchards near Delhi and also restored 30 old gardens of Alauddin. He also took measures to improve the quality of fruits in his orchards.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was ‘Dar-ul-Shafa’ established by Firuz Tughluq?
questions.explanation: Firuz Tughluq opened charitable hospital known a 'Dar-ul-Shafa' and also placed qualifi ed Hakeems in it.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Sultan of Delhi Sultanate established a charitable hospital named 'Dar-ul-Shifa"?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following dynasties ruled over India after the invasion of Timur?
questions.explanation: The invasion of Timur (1398 A.D.) destroyed both Delhi Sultanate as well as the Tughluq dynasty. Tughluq dynasty came to an end in 1412 A.D., after that, Daulat Khan became the new Sultan of Delhi in 1413 A.D. However, Khizr Khan defeated him who was the Governor of Lahore, appointed by Timur. He founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Sultans founded a town where now stands Agra?
questions.explanation: Nizam Khan, the third son of Bahlul Lodi, ascended the throne assuming the title of Sikandar Lodi on 17 July, 1489. Sikandar Lodi was the greatest among the three Lodi rulers. Sikandar Lodi is especially remembered for founding the city of Agra in 1504 A.D. with the purpose of controlling over the rulers of Rajasthan. His administration was noted for its effi ciency. Roads were made safe and irrigational facilities were provided for the benefi t of the peasantry. He knew Persian poetry. He used to write poems under the nickname 'Gulrukhi'. He was known to be a kind and generous ruler who cared for his subjects.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Identify the fi rst ruler of Vijaynagara who captured Goa from Bahamani’s?
questions.explanation: After the death of Bukka in 1377 A.D., his son, Hariharaa-II ascended to the throne. He assumed the title of “Maharajadhiraja” and conquered the region of Canara, Mysore, and Kanchi, Trichanapali and collected tax from the king of Sri Lanka. His major achievement was winning the Belgaum and Goa from Bahamani. He was the devotee of Virupaksha form of Lord Shiva.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the founder of Vijayanagara Empire?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara Empire was established during the reign in the year 1336 A.D. by two brothers named Harihara and Bukka. The capital of this kingdom was Hampi, which was situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: With whom the king of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya fought the battle of Golconda?
questions.explanation: The battle of Golconda was fought between the king of Vijayanagara, Krishnadeva Raya and the Sultan of Golconda, Quli Qutb Shah. Sultan Quli Qutb Shah founded the Qutb Shahi Dynasty in Golconda. Quli Qutb Shah expanded his kingdom by capturing forts at Warangal, Kondaveedu at a time when Krishnadeva Raya was busy fi ghting with the rulers of Orissa. Quli’s campaign against Krishnadeva Raya continued, but fi nally, he was defeated by him.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following King's region Persian traveller 'Abdur Razzak' came to India?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Persian ambassador Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Devaraya- II (1422-46 A.D.). Devaraya-II belonged to Sangama dynasty.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which famous war took place in 1565 A.D.?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The battle of Talikota (1565 A.D.), a watershed battle, was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Deccan Sultanates resulted in the defeat of Vijayanagara and ended weakening one of the greatest Indian empires originating from southern India before the Maratha Empire. Talikota is situated in Karnataka near Vijayapura city.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the chief characteristic of the fi nancial system of Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara kings enjoyed a massive income from various sources like land revenue, wealth tax, trade tax, commercial tax, tax on industry, social and community tax and fi ne charged on crime. The main source of income was from land revenue which was fi xed after the land was measured and categorized. The tax, namely ‘Shisth’ (Rai-Rekha) was the main source of income to the state. The revenue department was known as ‘Athavane.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The remains of Vijayanagara Empire are found in?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The ruins of Hampi (situated in central Karnataka) represent the ancient capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. The Virupaksha temple, located in Hampi, was built during the Vijayanagara period. Hampi is a UNESCO world heritage site.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following famous rulers founded a suburban township of Nagalapuram, near Vijayanagara, after his mother's name?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: The suburban township of Nagalapuram, near Vijayanagara was founded by Krishnadevaraya of the Vijayanagara Empire in memory of his mother Nagala Devi.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: During the Delhi Sultanate, the designation 'Muqaddam or Chaudhari' was used for

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: 'Muqaddam or Chaudhari' was village headman and in this capacity only was the highest revenue authority in the village and not just any revenue offi cial or village accountant.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: 'Diwan-i-Arz' department was associated with:
questions.explanation: The correctly matched departments and their activities are as follows : Diwan-i-Arz - Dealt with Military department Diwan-i-Risalat - Dealt with religious issues/ matters/related to foreign matters. Diwan-i-Insha - Dealt with State correspondence Diwan-i-Wizarat - Dealt with fi nancial matters

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following indicates taxes levied on the land product? i. Kharaj ii. Khums iii. Ushr iv. Muktai Select your answer from the following codes –
questions.explanation: In Islamic traditions, Khums refers to the historically required religious delegation of the Muslim army to pay one-fi fth of the spoils of war, the booty collected from non-believers after a military campaign.This tax was paid to the caliph or sultan, representing the state of Islam. The rest of the others are taxes levied on the land product.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Zawabits were concerned with :
questions.explanation: Zawabits were related to state laws in the administrative vocabulary of the Sultanate period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Coins-Tanka, Shashgani and Jital of Sultanate period was made of which of the following metals-
questions.explanation: Iltutmish was the fi rst to issue regular currency and declare Delhi as the capital of his empire. He started the ‘Tanka’ and the ‘Jital’ coins made up of silver and copper respectively in the Sultanate period. Shashgani was also a silver coin. The ratio of tanka and jital was 1:48.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri forms which entrance to the Jama Masjid?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Buland Darwaza is a fi fteen story high gateway that acts as the southern entrance of the Fatehpur Sikri city. It is higher than the courtyard of the Jama Masjid. Buland Darwaza popularly known as the 'Gate of Magnifi cence' was built by the Akbar to commemorate his victory over Gujarat.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Sultan built Alai Darwaza?
questions.explanation: The ‘Alai Darwaza is the main gate on the south of the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque at the Qutb Minar premises. It has a domed entrance which was constructed using red sandstone and is adorned with white marble. It was completed in 1311 A.D. by Turkish craftsmen. It is one of the fi rst buildings in India in Islamic architectural style.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the author of Tabaqat-i-Nasiri?
questions.explanation: The text ‘Tabaqat-i-Nasiri’ written by Minhaz-us-Siraj, was dedicated to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud. The text is divided into 23 volumes and was translated by H.G. Raverty into the English language. The text describes the victory of Muhammad Ghori over India.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The earliest description of Bakhtiyar Khalji's invasion of Bihar is in:

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is a medieval text by Minhaj-i-Siraj. It is an important sourcebook for the reconstruction of the history of the foundation of Muslim rule in Bengal. Pieces of evidence in the literature suggest that in 1193, Nalanda University was sacked by Bakhtiyar Khalji a Turk. The Persian Historian Minhaj-i-Siraj in his chronicle Tabaqat-i-Nasiri reported that thousands of monks were burned alive and thousands beheaded as Khalji tried his best to uproot Buddhism.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Muhammad Ghori was defeated by the Chaulukyas of Gujarat in

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Muhammad Ghori was defeated in 1178 by Bhimdev Solanki II, the Chalukya vanshi king of Gujarat.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Sultan demanded half the crops on land after measurement as revenue?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mohammad-Bin-Tughluq is considered an ill-fated idealist owing to his ambitious schemes and novel experiments which ended in miserable failures because they were all far ahead of their time. To overcome fi nancial diffi culties, Muhammad-Bin-Tughluq increased the land revenue to half the produce on the farmers of Doab (land between Ganges and Yamuna rivers) but Demand was based on expected production while Alauddin Khalji had fi xed the land revenue on the half of the produce of the land-based on measurement.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following rulers divided his troops into units of two hundred, two hundred fi fty and fi ve hundred?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Islam Shah was the son of Sher Shah. He ruled over North India roughly for 8 years and died in 1553 AD. He divided his army battalions into the units of fi fty, two hundred, two hundred fi fty and fi ve hundred.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which city of India was called 'Shiraz-i-Mashriq' (Shiraz of the East) in the medieval age?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The city of Jaunpur in India was called 'Shiraj-i-Mashriq' (Shiraz of the East) as it was a very important city for education and commerce in the region.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who laid the foundation of new landed aristocracy in Bengal?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Murshid Quli Khan, the Nawab of Bengal, replaced Mughal Jagirdari system of revenue with Maljasmani or Malzamini revenue system or Ijara system by which contracts were given for collection of revenue. Later, these contractors squeezed out Jagirdars and came to be known as Zamindars which formed a new landed aristocracy in Bengal.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Provincial Dynasty of North India and Deccan Province
questions.question: Who was the founder of Bahamani Kingdom?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bahamani Kingdom was founded by Alauddin Hasan Gangu by revolting against the Delhi 'Sultanate'. In 1347, the successful revolt of the new nobles against Muhammad Tughluq resulted in the founding of the Bahamani Dynasty. After his coronation, he assumed the title of 'Abul Hasan Mujaff ar Alauddin Bahman Shah'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: A common feature to all Bhakti Saints was that they –

options.a: Composed their verses in the language understood by their followers
options.b: Rejected the authority of the priestly class
options.c: Encouraged women to go to the temples

questions.answer_text: Composed their verses in the language understood by their followers
questions.explanation: The conduct of Bhakti saints was of a very high standard. Many of them visited the country and met many people having diff erent views. They also contributed to the advancement of Hindi, Kannada, Punjabi, Bengali, Telugu, Tamil and other languages. The Saints of the Bhakti movement gave their verses in regional and local languages so that their followers could easily understand them. This was the main reason behind the development of local languages.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi was refused an audience by Nizamuddin Auliya?
questions.explanation: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya saw the regime of more than seven Sultans, but he never visited their court. Sultan Jalaluddin tried to meet Nizamuddin Auliya through Amir Khusrau but when Nizamuddin Auliya heard that the Sultan was about to come, he moved to Ajodhan. When Alauddin asked him to meet, then Shaikh replied: “There are two doors in my home, if the Sultan comes from one door, I will go out by another.” He was also known as ‘Mehboob-e-Ilahi.’

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which Sufi order was Sufi Saint Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri associated?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sufi Saint Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri was associated with Firdausi Sufi order of Bihar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakaria belonged to which sect?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Shaikh Bahauddin Zakaria started Suhrawardi sect in India. Shaikh Sadr-ud-din Arif, Shaikh Rakh-ud-din Abul Fateh and Shaikh Jalaluddin Surkh were associated with this Sufi sect.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who composed ‘Barahmasa’?
questions.explanation: Barahmasa, Padmavat, Akharavat and Aakhri Kalaam are some of the texts written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. Among his texts, Padmavat has an important place in Hindi literature. Barahmasa is a part of Padmavat.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The main reason for Babur’s victory in the battle of Panipat was –
questions.explanation: The fi rst battle of Panipat was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi on 21 April, 1526. The main reason for Babur’s victory in the battle of Panipat was his skilled warfare. The army of Babur was smaller than the army of Ibrahim Lodi, even then he won the battle with the help of his eff ective warfare policy. Babur noted, “Ibrahim Lodi was an inexperienced young man careless in his movements, who marched without order, halted or retired without method and engaged without foresight.”

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which of the following battles are the main opponents not correctly stated?

options.a: Battle of Haldighati-Maharana Pratap and Akbar
options.b: First Battle of Panipat-Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
options.c: Second Battle of Panipat-Tipu Sultan and Marathas
options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.answer_text: Second Battle of Panipat-Tipu Sultan and Marathas
questions.explanation: The Battle of Haldighati was fought on 18 June 1576 between forces of Mewar led by Maharana Pratap and forces of Mughals (Akbar) led by Man Singh I of Ambar. The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between the invading forces of Babur and Ibrahim Lodi of Lodi Empire. The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between King of Delhi Hem Chandra Vikramaditya, popularly known as Hemu and army of Akbar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In which language was Tuzuk-i-Baburi’ written?
questions.explanation: The founder of the Mughal Empire, Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur wrote his memoirs (autobiography) ‘Tuzuk-i-Baburi’ also known as Baburnama written in Turkish language containing related events of his life.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Consider the following statements : The arrival of Babur into India led to the 1. introduction of gunpowder in the subcontinent 2. introduction of arch and dome in the region’s architecture 3. establishment of Timurid dynasty in the region 4. introduction of cannons in warfare Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Gunpowder entered India before Babur. It was used to demolish Fort's wall. But credit for using it in cannons and guns goes to Babur. Babur descended from Turk-Mongol conqueror Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side. Babur, the eldest son of Umar Shaikh Mirza, was born on 14th February, 1483. He ascended the throne in Ferghana in June, 1494. His accession saw the beginning of Timurid dynasty in the region. He established the Mughal dynasty in India after the victory at Panipat in 1526. Arch and Dome were already introduced during the Sultanate period.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who wrote Humayun Nama?
questions.explanation: Gulbadan Begum was the daughter of Babur. She was born in 1523 A.D. and died in 1603 A.D. She documented many historical events in her book ‘Humayun Nama’. Akbar had great respect for her. Gulbadan Begum wrote that she had written the history of Babur and Humayun on the orders of Akbar. She described the battle between Humayun and Kamran in her book.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Arrange properly as per dates of four important battles fought by Humayun, the names of battlefi elds are given below –
questions.explanation: The correct order of battles fought by Humayun is as follows-Devara, Chausa, Kanauj and Sirhind. Humayun defeated Afghan rebels on the banks of Gomati at Devara or Daurah in 1532 A.D. Sher Shah defeated Humayun in the Battle of Chausa on 26 June 1539 in which a water fetcher named Nizam saved his life. This victory against Humayun increased the prestige and power of Sher Shah. He read ‘Khutba’ by his name occupying the title of Sher Shah and engraved this on the coins. On 17 May, 1540 Humayun was again defeated by Sher Shah in the Battle of Kanauj (Bilgram) and Humayun fl ed from one place to the other after this war. Humayun occupied Delhi again in the Battle of Sirhind on 22 June, 1555.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: "No government not even the British has shown so much wisdom as this Pathan." Who wrote these words about Sher Shah Suri?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: H.G. Keen writes about Sher Shah Suri "No government, not even the British has shown as much wisdom as this Pathan". In fact, this comment about Sher Shah Suri was made because in a very short time, he snatched the reins of power from the Mughals in India and took it into his own hands.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following rulers at fi rst assumed the title of ‘Hazrat-e-Ala’ and afterward ‘Sultan’?
questions.explanation: In 1534 A.D., Sher Khan assumed the title of ‘Hazrat-e-Ala’ after defeating the ruler of Bengal, Nusrat Shah. He assumed the royal title of ‘Sher Shah’ after defeating Humayun in the Battle of Chausa on June 26, 1539 and ordered to read Khutba by his name and the coins to be minted in his name.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where is Sher Shah’s tomb located ?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sher Shah's tomb is built on a high platform in the middle of a pond at a place called Sasaram in Rohtas district of Bihar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: When Humayun invaded Chunar Fort fi rst time ?
questions.explanation: Humayun invaded Chunar Fort for the fi rst time in 1532 A.D. Humayun besieged this fort for four months after that Sher Khan accepted his supremacy. In addition to this, he invaded Kalinjar in 1531 A.D. and annexed Raisina fort in 1532 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following made an off er to Humayun that he would surrender Bihar and pay an annual tribute of 10 lakh dinars if he was allowed to retain Bengal?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Sher Khan made an off er to Mughal emperor Humayun that he would surrender Bihar and pay an annual tribute of about 10 lakh dinars if he was allowed to retain Bengal but Humayun declined the off er.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following has constructed mausoleum for his emperor husband ?
questions.explanation: Haji Begum constructed mausoleum for her husband Humayun at Delhi during 1565-72 A.D. as ‘tomb of Humayun.’ Mirak Mirza Ghiyath (Ghiyas), a Persian, was the architect, employed by Haji Begum for this tomb. It is the fi rst dome mausoleum of India made up of white marble. A garden is surrounded outwards of the tomb.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among these rulers divided his troops into units of two hundred, two hundred and fi fty and fi ve hundred?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/ More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Islam Shah was the son of Sher Shah. Islam Shah ruled the whole of North India for about 8 years. He divided his troops into units of two hundred, two hundred fi fty and fi ve hundred. Probably this system of military division was prevalent even during the time of Sher Shah. It is to be known that the Bihar Public Service Commission has considered answer (e) to this question.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the commander of Rana Pratap’s army in the Battle of Haldighati?
questions.explanation: Hakim Khan Sur was the commander of Rana Pratap’s army in the Battle of Haldighati. He was a Pathan adventurer, a member of the Sur dynasty who commanded an army of 5,000 Afghans in the battle of Haldighati on 18 June, 1576.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Yousuf Shah Chak, the last Muslim ruler of Kashmir valley, who was exiled to Bihar by the Mughal emperor Akbar, was buried in –

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Yousuf Shah Chak was a ruler of Kashmir. Yousuf was exiled to Bihar by Mughal emperor Akbar. He died in Jagannath Puri (Odisha) and was buried in Biswak (Nalanda).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who of the following Muslim rulers abolished the pilgrimage tax?
questions.explanation: Akbar abolished Jizya, the pilgrimage tax and Slavery in 1564, 1563 & 1562 respectively. Under his liberal religious policy.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Zabti system was introduced by –
questions.explanation: Zabti System was introduced for land revenue in the reign of Akbar which was based on schedules of Dustur-ul-Amal and Zabti Khasre for land survey and land revenue determination. Most of the area was based on this system.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who promulgated Din-e-Elahi?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Akbar launched "Tauhid-i-Ilahi" or "Din-i-Ilahi" (Din-e-Elahi) in 1582 A.D. Din-i-Ilahi was a syncretic religion which intended to merge the best elements of all the religions of the community. Indeed, the prophet of this new sect was Abul Fazl. Among Hindus, only Birbal accepted Din-i-Ilahi. Raja Bhagawan Das and Man Singh bluntly refused to embrace Din-i-Ilahi.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: European paintings were introduced in the court of :

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: European paintings were introduced in the court of Akbar for fi rst time.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: 'Daswant and Basawan' famous painters were courtier of Mughal emperor :

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Abul Fazal had listed 15 outstanding painters in his text Ain-i-Akbari-Daswant, Basawan, Keshav Lal, Mukund Miskin, Madhes, Jagan, Mahesh, Khemaran, Tara, Sanwal, Harivansh.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the ruler of India when the English East India Company was formed?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The English East India Company was formed in the year 1600 A.D. Elizabeth was the Empress of England and Akbar was emperor of India at that time.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Akbar merged Bengal and Bihar in his empire :
questions.explanation: Daud Khan succeeded his father Suleman Karrani in 1572 A.D. after his death. Daud Khan invaded Patna Mughal fort after declaring himself an independent ruler. Akbar ordered Munim Khan to suppress this revolt and occupy Bihar. Munim Khan defeated Daud Khan in a battle and annexed Bihar in 1574 A.D. Daud fl ed away to Bengal after his defeat. On 12 July, 1576 Todarmal, defeated Daud. Thus, Akbar merged Bengal and Bihar in his empire in 1576 A.D.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Ain-e-Akbari was written by -

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ain-e-Akbari is written by Abul Fazal one of the Navratnas of Akbar. This is the third part of the 'Akbar Nama' It contains the offi cial account of Akbar's administration.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Tabaqat-i-Akbari, which has been sometimes considered more reliable than Abul Fazl's Akbarnama, was written by

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Khwaja Nizamuddin Ahmad wrote Tabaqat-i-Akbari. Gulbadan Begum wrote Humayun-Nama while Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote Padshahnama.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: "After uniting India, he wanted to unite the Mid-East and Western Asia with him as a very important step towards the establishment of a world empire." R. P. Tripathi wrote it about which ruler of Mughal India?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: R.P. Tripathi writes about Mughal Emperor Akbar that "After uniting India, he wanted to unite the Mid-East and Western Asia with him a very important step towards the establishment of a world empire."

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who introduced ‘Do-aspa and Sih-aspa’ system?
questions.explanation: ‘Do-aspa and Sih-aspa’ system was introduced by Jahangir. Under the provision of this system, Mansabdars had to maintain an excess number of soldiers without increment in rank (zat). Do-aspa : In this system, Mansabdars had to maintain double horses in comparison to their ‘Sawar’ rank. Sih-aspa : In this system, Mansabdars had to maintain a triple the number of horses in comparison to their ‘Sawar’ rank.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Whom of the following Englishmen did Jahangir respected with title ‘English Khan’?
questions.explanation: Hawkins was the fi rst English sent by English East India Company to visit the court of Jahangir in 1608 A.D. Jahangir was so much impressed by Hawkins that he gave him the title of ‘English Khan’ and also made him marry a lady from Armenia.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Itmad-ud-Daula’s tomb at Agra was built by
questions.explanation: Tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula was built by Noorjahan (Nur Jahan) at Agra between 1622-1628 after the death of his father. This elegant monument is located on the bank of river Yamuna. The main mausoleum is built with white marble. Itmad-ud-Daula has a special place in the chronicles of both history as well as architecture. The monument is priceless because this is the fi rst tomb in India that is entirely made up of marble. Inspite of marble and inlay work, it was for the fi rst time that a new style of ornamentation, Pietradura, was used.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: During the time of which Mughal Emperor did Sir Thomas Roe come to India?

options.e: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sir Thomas Roe reached Surat in September 1615 AD as an envoy of King James I of England, he attended the court of Mughal ruler Jahangir in Ajmer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: What was the root of the dispute between the Shah of Iran and Mughal rulers?
questions.explanation: Qandahar was the cause of dispute between the Shah of Iran and the Mughal rulers of Qandahar because it became an issue of prestige for Persians and Mughals. The expansion of colonialism of both the dynasties was mostly depended on suzerainty of Qandahar.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who made the Red Fort in Delhi?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan transferred his capital from Agra to Delhi and laid the foundations of Shahjahanabad in his name. Red Fort is an important monument of Shah Jahan. It is an irregular octagon with two long sides on the west and east and with two main gates, one on the west and the other on the south called Lahori and Delhi gates respectively. It is unique in architecture and glory.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following historians declared the regime of Shah Jahan to be the Golden Era of the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: Dr. A.L. Srivastava wrote in his book ‘‘Mughalkaleen Bharat (1526-1803)’’ that the regime of Shah Jahan is the golden period in the medieval history of India. However, it is true only on the basis of art and especially architecture. J.N. Sarkar and V.A. Smith are not in favour to accept this fact, but R.S. Sharma also accepted this fact. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the fi rst Mughal ruler who fought against the British?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The fi rst confl ict between the Mughals and the british took place in 1686 A.D. during the reign of Aurangzeb. The Mughal governor Shaistha Khan had driven the British out of Hooghly, including Jab Charock.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The meaning of ‘Jihad’ carried on by Aurangzeb is –
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb was a Sunni Muslim. Aurangzeb tried to enforce the Quranic law, according to which enjoins upon every pious muslim to carry on Jihad (holy wars) against non-Muslim lands (Dar-ul-Harb) till they are converted to Islam (Dar-ul-Islam).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who wrote Alamgir-Nama?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Alamgir-nama, a history of fi rst ten years of Aurangzeb's reign was compiled by Mirza Muhammad Kazim.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the Mughal administration ‘Muhtasib’ was –

options.c: An Offi cer-in-Charge of public morals

questions.answer_text: An Offi cer-in-Charge of public morals
questions.explanation: Muhtasib, the censor of public morals acted as police cum Judge in the observance of the law by the Muslims.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: In medieval India, why was the mansabdari system introduced?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Akbar introduced a well-organised system in the military and civil service of the empire which came to be known as Mansabdari system. The main intention to introduce Mansabdari was to provide a clean and better administration.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: ‘Madad-i-Mash’ indicates in Mughal administration –

options.b: Revenue freeland granted to learned person
options.c: Pension provided to military offi cials

questions.answer_text: Revenue freeland granted to learned person
questions.explanation: Sometimes, the Mughal administration issued grants as a Madad-i-Mash to pious or otherwise worthy recipients as charity. The spirit of composite culture and harmony was expressed in revenue-free grants (Madad-i-Mash), which the nobles extended to the support of saints, maintenance of religious institutions, religious places and upkeep of Mashaikhs, etc.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: The meaning of word Bantai during Medieval period was?
questions.explanation: The meaning of word ‘Bantai’ during the medieval period was a system of calculating revenue in which real produce was distributed between state and peasants. Sher Shah Suri opted 3 systems for calculating revenue : Nasq/Muktai/Kankut Nakadi or Jabti Galla Bakshi or Bantai Bantai was of 3 types (i) Khet Bantai (ii) Lank Bantai (iii) Raasi Bantai.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Music and Paintings of Mughal Period
questions.question: Who did illustrate “Dastan-e-Amir Hamza”?
questions.explanation: Most of the Mughals were renowned as great patrons of arts. The fi rst endeavor was to complete the pictures of the earliest Mughal illustrated manuscript, the Dastan-e-Amir Hamza began in the period of Humayun. It took 15 years to fi nish under the supervision of Mir Sayyid Ali and then Abdus Samad more than 50 artists completed it.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Music and Paintings of Mughal Period
questions.question: Mughal painting reached its zenith under –

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Jahangir had an artistic inclination. During his reign, Mughal painting developed further as Jahangir was fascinated with art, science and architecture from a young age. He showed a leaning towards painting and had an atelier of his own. His interest in portraiture led to much development in this art form. The art of Mughal painting reached great heights during Jahangir’s reign. His interest in painting also served his scientifi c interest in nature. Painter Ustad Mansur became one of the best artists to document the animals and plants which Jahangir either encountered on his military expeditions or received as donations. Jahangir maintained a huge aviary and kept a record of every specimen and organized experiments. He patronized the European and Persian arts.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Music and Paintings of Mughal Period
questions.question: Which Mughal ruler established Karkhanas for painting?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Akbar was very fond of painting and during his reign painting was organised as an imperial establishment or Karkhana called Tasvir Khana where the painters worked. So option (b) is correct option.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.chapter_name: Music and Paintings of Mughal Period
questions.question: Arrange properly as per dates of four important battles fought by Humayun, the names of battlefi elds are given below –
questions.explanation: The correct order of battles fought by Humayun is as follows-Devara, Chausa, Kanauj and Sirhind. Humayun defeated Afghan rebels on the banks of Gomati at Devara or Daurah in 1532 A.D. Sher Shah defeated Humayun in the Battle of Chausa on 26 June 1539, in which a water fetcher named Nizam saved his life. This victory against Humayun increased the prestige and power of Sher Shah. He read ‘Khutba’ by his name occupying the title of Sher Shah and engraved this on the coins. On 17 May, 1540 Humayun was again defeated by Sher Shah in the Battle of Kanauj (Bilgram) and Humayun fl ed from one place to the other after this war. Humayun occupied Delhi again in the Battle of Sirhind on 22 June, 1555.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which among the following ports was called Babul Makka (Gate of Makka) during the Mughal period?
questions.explanation: During the Mughal period, pilgrims used to visit Mecca for Haj from Surat. Hence, Surat was known as 'Mecca dwar', 'Babul Mecca' (Gate of Mecca) and 'Meccabari'.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Sultan was reputed to be 'Akbar of Kashmir'?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama arrived on western-coast port of Calicut in 1498 A.D. He discovered a new and all sea route to India and he was welcomed by Zamorin, the then king of Calicut. The voyage of Vasco da Gama opened the new trade dimensions of the Indo-Portuguese alliance. Vasco da Gama earned 60 times more profi t in Europe by black pepper trade from India, which encouraged other Portuguese traders. The Portuguese merchants established their commercial fi rms in India at the ports of Calicut, Goa, Daman, Diu and Hooghly. Vasco da Gama revisited India in 1502. Francisco de Almeida came to India in 1505 as the fi rst Portuguese Viceroy and Albuquerque came to India in 1509 after him as a new Viceroy. He annexed Goa in 1510 from Bijapur ruler Adil Shah. The Portuguese maintained Goa as the epicentre of their culture and entity.

questions.explanation: The First Carnatic War (1746-48 A.D.) was an off shoot of the Anglo-French rivalry in the Austrian War of Succession that took place in Europe in 1740 A.D. The British Captain Bernett captured some French ships which became the immediate cause of war. Nawab Anwaruddin sent an army under the command of Mahfooz Khan to besiege the French in Madras during the First Carnatic War. The French Army (under command of Captain Paradise) defeated Nawab’s Army at the Battle of St. Thome near Adyar river. Treaty of Aix-Le-Chapelle (18 Oct, 1748) ended the War of Austrian succession and with it fi rst Carnatic War ended and the Britishers reoccupied Madras. The fi rst Carnatic War is memorable for War of St. Thome.

He was assigned Allahabad and Kada ceded by the Nawab of Oudh. The Emperor issued an order dated 12th August, 1765 granting Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. During this time Robert Clive was Governor of East India Company in Bengal. The emperor’s order legalized the political authority of Company in Bengal and British rule expanded all over India including Delhi. Successors of Shah Alam-II i.e. Akbar-II (1806-37) and Bahadurshah-II (1837-57) became pensioners of East India Company.

questions.explanation: According to the second Treaty of Allahabad (August, 1765), Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II was taken under the Company’s protection and had to reside at Allahabad. Shah Alam II conferred Diwani (fi scal revenue collection authority) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company by issuing ‘Farman’ on 12 August, 1765. In return, the company had to pay the emperor an annual sum of Rs 26 Lakhs as pension. At that time, the Company was neither interested in taking responsibility for tax revenue collection nor it was capable of doing so. Therefore, the Company appointed two Diwans- Mohammad Raza Khan for Bengal and Raja Shitab Rai for Bihar. Thus, all business of Diwani and Nizamat was conducted by Indians but authorized by the British Company.

questions.question: Lord Lytton is not associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton was an English politician who served as the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880. His tenure as Viceroy was marked by a controversial policy known as the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, which aimed to regulate the Indian vernacular press and limit its freedom of expression. The policies introduced included the Indian Arms Act of 1878, according to which, it was a criminal off ense for Indians to carry arms without a license. The Act was discriminatory as it did not apply to the British, Anglo-Indians, Europeans, and certain government personnel. Famine Codes were given by the Famine Commission that was set up in 1878 under the Chairmanship of Sir Richard Strachey (Strachey Commission) during tenure of Lord Lytton only. The infamous 'Famine Codes', have been criticized for their handling of the 1876-1878 famine in India, which resulted in signifi cant loss of life. Ilbert bill on the other hand was introduced in 1883 by Lord Rippon that allowed Indian Judges and Magistrates to try British Off enders in criminal cases at district level.

In 1803 AD, Shah Shuja (the grandson of Ahmad Shah Abdali) sat on the throne of Kabul but Shah Mahmud (brother of Shah Shuja) along with powerful Barekzay chieftain Fateh Khan and Dost Muhammad dethroned him and occupied Kashmir and Peshawar. questions.question: It focussed on the actual needs of the Provinces. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: The Indian Council Act of 1861 implemented the strategy of legislative devolution, and the probable outcome of this was Mayo's Resolution of 1870, focusing on fi nancial decentralization. The Imperial Government, prompted by administrative effi ciency and fi nancial constraints, opted to transfer the control of certain administrative departments - including education, medical services, and roads - to provincial governments. This marked the inception of local fi nancial management. To ensure fi scal stability, provincial governments were granted the authority to rely on local taxation to balance their budgets. Lord Mayo's resolution had delineated - "Local interest, supervision, and care are necessary to success in the management of the funds devoted to education, sanitation, medical relief, and local public works. The operation of this resolution in its full meaning and integrity will aff ord opportunities for the development of self-government, for strengthening municipal institution, and for the association of Natives and Europeans to a greater extent than heretofore in the administration of aff airs."

questions.question: The policy of 'Security Cell' is related to-
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings and Wellesley were related to the security cell or Ring Fence policy. Warren Hastings waged war with Mysore and Marathas, in the spirit of achieving equal status with other Indian princely states. At this time the Company tried to form a buff er state around its state. Its purpose was only to protect our state or we can also say that protect the borders of our neighboring states so that our borders are safe. At that time the fear was mainly from Afghans and Marathas. Therefore, the Company took over the task of arranging the defence of Awadh on the condition that the Nawab of Awadh should bear the burden of that expenditure and thus the defense of Awadh was the defense of Bengal. The arrival of Wellesley marked a change in the Company's relations with the Indian princely states. Wellesley's aimed to force the Indian princely states to depend on the Company for their defence. He tried to bring the Indian princely states under British political power and military protection. Following are the major British policies towards the princely states 1. Company's struggle for equality with Indian princely states (1740–1765 A.D.) 2. 'Safety Cell' policy or Ring fence policy (1765-1813 A.D.) 3. Subordinate separation policy (1813-1857 A.D.) 4. Subordinate union policy (1858-1935 A.D.) 5. Policy of Union of Equals (1935-1947 A.D.)

questions.question: First Maratha Sardar to accept the subsidiary alliance of Lord Wellesley was-
questions.explanation: The subsidiary alliance system was introduced in India by Lord Wellesley. The main principles of a subsidiary alliance were – 1. An Indian ruler entering into a subsidiary alliance with the British had to accept British forces within his territory and also agree to pay for their maintenance. 2. The ruler would accept a British resident in his state. 3. An Indian ruler who entered into a subsidiary alliance would not enter into any further alliance with any other power. 4. The ruler would not employ any Europeans other than the British. 5. In case of a confl ict with any other state, he would agree to the resolution decided by the British. 6. The ruler would acknowledge East India Company as the paramount power in India. 7. In return for the ruler accepting its conditions, the company undertook the protection of the state from external dangers and disorders. 8. If the Indian ruler failed to make the payments required by the alliance, then part of its territory was to be taken away as a penalty. The Nizam of Hyderabad was the fi rst to enter into such an alliance. The Nawab of Awadh was next to accept the alliance, and Maratha ruler Bajirao II (1802 A.D.) also accepted a subsidiary alliance. Several states like Hyderabad (1798 A.D.), Tanjore and Mysore (1799 A.D.), Awadh (1801 A.D.), Bhonsle (1803 A.D.), Sindhiya (1804 A.D.), Holkar (1818 A.D.) adopted this system.

questions.question: When was the new Enfi eld Rifl e with greased cartridges introduced in the British Indian Army?
questions.explanation: The Company decided to use new Enfi eld Rifl e instead of old Brown Bess gun in December, 1856. The training for the use of this rifl e was organized in Dum Dum, Ambala, and Sialkot. The rifl e needed an extraordinary kind of loading of a cartridge in the magazine and hence the soldiers while in the ensuing fi ght, had to bite off the outer covering of the cartridge while loading it down into the rifl e’s muzzle. The cartridge was rumoured to have been greased with animal fat (Pig fat and Cow fat). Army Commanders refused rumours without any cross-checking, but the soldiers were of the view that this was an intentional act of the British to besmirch their religion. This became the immediate cause fi rst Independence Struggle of India in 1857.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following was not a reason for making the sepoys of the East India Company rebellious?

options.a: The eff orts of the offi cers of the company to spread Christianity
options.b: The order to the sepoys to travel on ships
options.d: The ineffi ciency of the offi cers
options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: The ineffi ciency of the offi cers
questions.explanation: The ineffi ciency of the offi cers was not a cause for the sepoy Mutiny. The Indian Rebellion of 1857 occurred as a result of an accumulation of factors over time, rather than any single event, like an eff ort of offi cers to spread Christianity among the soldiers led to interference in the religious matters of the people. The order of the Company to the sepoys to travel on a ship was another reason as in Hinduism it was believed that travelling on the sea can devoid them of their religious status of being a Hindu. A more immediate cause of the sepoy’s dissatisfaction was the recent order that they would not be given the foreign service allowance (Bhatta/ Batta) when serving in Sindh or Punjab and rumours of the use of animal fat in the cartridges of the New Enfi eld Rifl e.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who spearheaded the 1857 Revolt in Bihar ?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kunwar Singh was one of the most important freedom fi ghters in the Sepoy Mutiny of 1857. Kunwar Singh was born in Jagdishpur in the Shahabad (now in Bhojpur District) of Bihar. He belonged to Arrah in Bihar during the mutiny. When the people of all parts of India rose against British authority in 1857, Babu Kunwar Singh was nearly eighty years old. In that age, he fought against the English East India Company. Despite his age and failing health, Kunwar Singh plunged into the thick of it and battled against the British forces with grim determination and undaunted courage. In Bihar, Kunwar Singh was the Leader against the British. He assumed command of the soldiers who had revolted at Danapur on 25th July, 1857. Two days later he occupied Arrah, the district headquarters. Major Vincent Eyre relieved the town on 3rd August, defeated Kunwar Singh’s force and destroyed Jagdishpur. Kunwar Singh left his ancestral village and reached Lucknow in December 1857. In March 1858, he occupied Azamgarh. However, he had to leave the place soon. He was pursued by Brigadier Douglas, and he retreated towards his home in Bihar. On 23 April, 1858 Kunwar Singh had a victory near Jagdishpur over the force led by Captain Le Grand, but on 26 April, 1858 the following day he died in his village. The mantle of the old chief now fell on his brother Amar Singh who, despite heavy odds, continued the struggle and for a considerable time ran a parallel government in the district of Shahabad (Now Bhojpur). In October 1859 Amar Singh joined the rebel leaders in the Nepal Terai.

questions.question: The Indigo Rebellion was about:

options.a: the peasant not wanting to grow indigo but being forced
options.b: the peasant wanting to grow indigo but being forced not to
options.c: the peasant not wanting to grow indigo but being forced to grow at a price that was unacceptable
options.d: a protest movement that carried and indigo-coloured fl ag
options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: the peasant not wanting to grow indigo but being forced to grow at a price that was unacceptable
questions.explanation: The Indigo Revolt (1859-60 A.D.) took place in Bengal immediately after the revolt of 1857. Sanyasi Rebellion occurred in 1763-1800 A.D., Santhal Rebellion occurred in 1855-56 A.D., and Pabna uprising took place in 1873- 76 A.D. Indigo Revolt began from Govindpur village of Nadia district in West Bengal led by two former employees of indigo producers. Digambar Viswas and Vishnu Viswas organized the peasants into a counterforce and refused to sow indigo. This indigo revolt of Bengal was directed against British planters who forced peasants to take advances and sign fraudulent contracts which forced the peasants to grow Indigo under terms that were least profi table to them. In September, 1859 all the cultivators revolted against the landlords. The agitation spread in regions like Nadia, Pabna, Khulna, Dhaka, Malda, Dinajpur, etc. All Indigo factories were shut down due to this strike. The intellectual class of Bengal expressed support to the Movement by their articles and rallies. The editor of “Hindu Patriot” Harishchandra Mukherjee played a signifi cant role in this agitation. This revolt was vividly portrayed by Dinbandhu Mitra in his play Neel Darpan.

questions.explanation: The rebels did not have many grievances against the ‘Whites’ or ‘Sahibs.’ Their main enemy was the ‘Dikus’ (government offi cers). Ten thousand Santhals assembled in the fi eld of Bhognadih on 30th June, 1855, and unanimously passed a resolution to fi ght the corrupt Government offi cials, the “Dikus.” The Dikus had betrayed them, forced them to slavery and abused their women; they had no choice but to fi ght them. They assembled under their leaders Sidhu, Kanu, Chand, Bhairav and pledged to fi ght till their independence. A small contingent of force under Major Burrough was called to suppress the rebels, but he met tremendous resistance and was defeated at Pirpainati. The victory of the Santhals over the almighty British further fuelled the rebellion and it spread like wildfi re.
