questions.question: The by-product of photosynthesis is :

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs in membrane-bound structures called the chloroplasts. The main product of photosynthesis is glucose, which is the molecule that produces energy to run the processes of the cell. Oxygen is mainly a by-product of photosynthesis.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The process in which atmospheric carbon dioxide is con-verted into carbohydrates during photosynthesis is

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: The process in which atmospheric carbon dioxide is converted into carbohydrates during photosynthesis is reduction.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Plants appear to bend towards light due to–

options.a: Concentration of auxins at shoot tip
options.b: Concentration of auxins at root tip
options.c: Diffusion of auxins towards shady side of shoot
options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.answer_text: Diffusion of auxins towards shady side of shoot
questions.explanation: ● The bending of plant towards light is known as phototropism. It is due to plant hormone auxins. When the growing parts of a phototropic plant detect sunlight, auxins (synthesized at the shoot tips) help the cells grow longer. ● When only one part is receiving the light, the Auxin hormone through diffusion moves to the part which is receiving less sunlight and helps in the elongation of cells that are receiving less sunlight.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which metal ion is found in chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Magnesium ion is found in chlorophyll, chlorophyll is the green photosynthetic pigment present in plants. It initiates the process of converting light energy into chemical energy through the process of photosynthesis.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Photosynthesis occurs in-
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis takes place primarily in leaves and partially in stems. It takes place within especialized cell structures called chloroplasts. A leaf has a petiole or the stalk and a lamina, the flat portion of the leaf. As its area is broad, the lamina helps in the absorption of sunlight and carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts that have chlorophyll present in them. It is the chlorophyll that absorbs light energy from the sun. There are tiny pores called stomata that function as roadways for carbon dioxide to enter and oxygen to leave the plant.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Solar energy is converted into ATP in :

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the process of photosynthesis solar energy is converted into ATP in chloroplast. In light reactions (energy-transduction reactions) of photosynthesis solar energy is converted into chemical energy in the form of two energy-transporting molecules, ATP and NADPH.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which among the following is a character of chloroplast which makes them qualified to self-replication?

options.a: Presence of both DNA and RNA
options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.answer_text: Presence of both DNA and RNA
questions.explanation: Presence of DNA and RNA both are a character of chloroplast makes them qualified to self-replication. Chloroplasts, the organelles responsible for photosynthesis are in many respects similar to mitochandria. Plant chloroplasts are like mitochandria are bounded by double membrane called the chloroplast envelope. In addition to this membrane chloroplasts have a third membrane called the Thylakoid membrane. The major difference between chloroplasts and mitochandria in terms of both structure and function is the Thylakoid membrane.

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: The pigment essential for nitrogen fixation by leguminous plants is called "leghemoglobin". It is a protein found in the root nodules of leguminous plants like soyabeans, peas etc. Leghemoglobin helps in creating an oxygen-free environment within the root nodules, which is crucial for the functioning of nitrogenase, the enzyme responsible for nitrogen fixation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Water is conducted in vascular plants by-
questions.explanation: The xylem transports water and soluble mineral nutrients from the roots throughout the plant. It is also used to replace water lost during transpiration and photosynthesis.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Water in plants is transported by :

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: There are two types of transporting tissues found in vascular plants. (i) Phloem and (ii) Xylem. Xylem is the specialised tissue of vascular plants that transports water and minerals from plants. Soil interface to stems and leaves and provides mechanical support and storage.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Water passes from the soil into the root by the physical process is called -

options.e: None of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: Water reaches the roots from the soil through the process of osmosis.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Water enters from soil into root hairs of plants due to

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Water enters the root hairs by the process of osmosis. Osmosis is the process by which the molecules of a solvent, such as water, move from a region of its higher concentration to a region of its lower concentration through a semipermeable membrane. This decreases the water potential inside the cell, so water molecules move down gradient into the cell.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is present in the intestine of termites to digest cellulose?

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Termites have cellulolytic enzyme in their gut to digest the cellulose. The protozoa break the cellulose into the simple sugar thereby termites are able to metabolize the cellulose. Termites eat wood, which is mostly cellulose which they can not digest without their symbiote gut protozoans.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Water reaches great heights in trees because of suction pull caused by

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Water reaches great heights in trees because of suction pull caused by Transpiration. Transpiration is the process in which water is lost as water vapor from the aerial parts of the plant through stomata. Transpiration is essential evaporation of water from the leaves of the plant. Transpiration is ultimately the main driver of water movement in Xylem. Transpiration is a passive process, meaning that ATP is not required for water movement.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Pneumatophores are present in

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.answer_text: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In some plants such as Rhizophora growing in swampy area, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards. Such roots called pneumatophores, help to get oxygen for respiration. Pneumatophores are present in hydrophytes, halophytes plants.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In how many steps CO2 is released in aerobic respiration?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration is the process that leads to a complete oxidation of organic substances in the presence of oxygen, and releases CO2 , water and a large amount of energy present in the substrate. This type of respiration is most common in higher organisms. In three steps CO2 is released in aerobic respiration. Those steps are: ● During acetyl CO - A formation ● During formation of alpha-Ketoglutaric acid in krebs cycle ● During succinic acid formation in krebs cycle.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which group are called the 'amphibians' of the plant kingdom?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom. Amphibians are those organisms which live on both land and in water.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an artificial ripening agent?
questions.explanation: Ethephon and ethylene both are useful as artificial ripening agents, the question is deleted.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Embryo is found in –
questions.explanation: The embryo along with other cells from the mother plant develops into the seed for the next generation, which, after germination, grows into a new plant.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Plants are formed like parent plant from –
questions.explanation: Plants are propagated by two methods – 1. Sexual propagation or seed propagation. 2. Asexual or vegetative propagation. Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction of a plant. Only one plant is involved and offspring is the result of one parent. The new plant is genetically identical to the parent. In this process, new organism arises from any vegetative port of the parent (root, stem, leaf etc.) and possesses exactly the same characteristics of the parent plant. The purity of plants is maintained in vegetative propagation which is not possible in sexual reproduction. Stem cutting, grafting, layering, etc. are common artificial methods of vegetative propagation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Stem cutting is done generally to grow –
questions.explanation: Botanically, Sugarcane belongs to the Andropogonae tribe of the family Gramineae. Sugarcane plants are propagated by stem cutting. Stem cutting is segmented parts of the stem or entire stems detached from the main branch. Mango and cotton are generally grown from seeds while suckers are used as the planting material for banana. Sucker in banana arises from the root and is an extension of the rhizome as a lateral root. Some farmers also practice tissue culture for banana cultivation using seedlings developed through tissue culture. Rhizomes and peepers are the other planting materials used for banana cultivation.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The stem of the plant helps in distributing food to all parts of the plant. It also helps in -

options.e: None of the above / more than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above / more than one of the above
questions.explanation: The stem of the plant helps to distribute food (nutrients along with water and store food (nutrients) to all parts of the plant. It plays the main role to supports the leaves, flowers and fruits of the plant as well as gives shape to the plant.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Pollination is best defined as –

options.a: transfer of pollen grain from anther to stigma
options.c: growth of pollen tube in ovule
options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: transfer of pollen grain from anther to stigma
questions.explanation: In pollination, the pollen grains of the flowers's anther are transferred to the pistil or stigma of the flower. This process is called pollination.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The anther contains
questions.explanation: The anther usually contains four pollen sacs which are responsible for producing pollen grains. Each pollen grain is a single cell containing two male.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Plants which flower only once in life are
questions.explanation: The term monocarpic defines those plants that flower a single time, set seeds for reproduction, and then die. There are annuals, biennials, and perennials in this category of plant material.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The most important part of the plant in term of its life cycle is–
questions.explanation: The flower is the most important part of the plant in term of its life cycle. The biological function of a flower is to mediate the union of male and female gametes in order to produce seeds. The process begins with pollination followed by fertilization and continues with the formation and dispersal of the seed.

questions.question: A plant is obtained like a mother plant -
questions.explanation: Like the mother plant, the plant comes from seed and cutting off the stem.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Name a clinical trial in which blood is transfused from recovered COVID-19 patient to a corona virus patient who is in critical condition.
questions.explanation: Convalescent plasma is a transfusion of blood plasma from someone who has recovered from COVID-19. Current evidence shows that convalescent plasma does not improve survival or reduce the need for mechanical ventilation, while it has significant costs.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How do COVID vaccines stimulate an immune re-sponse?

options.a: By introducing live attenuated SARS-CoV-2 virus
options.b: By introducing a real SARS-CoV-2 virus
options.c: By introducing a harmless piece of SARS-CoV-2 virus
options.d: By introducing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 virus

questions.answer_text: By introducing live attenuated SARS-CoV-2 virus
questions.explanation: 'Covaxin' falls under this category i.e. Inactivated or attenuated live virus. 'Covishield' apparently fall under this category but it is a viral vector vaccine that uses an adenovirus found in Chimpanzees, ChADOX1 and not SARS-CoV-2 virus. So correct option is (a).

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following does not have any enzyme in its cells?

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.answer_text: None of the above/More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Lichen, bacteria and algae, all these have enzymes in their cells. The virus generally relies on the enzymes already pres-ent in the host cell or make enzymes that it needs using its own genome inside the host cell. Some viruses have no enzymes at all inside the viral particle itself. In other viruses, a small number of enzymes can be found inside the viral particle itself and also on the surface of some viruses. Enzymes found in some viral particles are reverse transcriptase, RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, an integrase, neuraminidase etc. Thus, the option (e) is the right answer.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The disease caused by HIV is –
questions.explanation: AIDS (Acquired immune deficiency syndrome or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) is a syndrome caused by a virus called HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) which destroys the disease resistance power of the human body. People infected with HIV may have the following symptoms : – Rapid weight loss – Recurring fever or profuse night sweats – Extreme and unexplained tiredness – Prolonged swelling of the lymph glands in the armpits, groin, or neck – Diarrhoea that lasts for more than a week – Sores of the mouth, anus, or genitals – Pneumonia – Red, brown, pink, or purplish blotches on or under the skin or inside the mouth, nose, or eyelids – Memory loss, depression, and other neurologic disorders.

questions.explanation: P-amino salicylic acid is an antimicrobial drug which is used for the treatment of both tuberculosis and leprosy. Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by bacteria “Mycobacterium tuberculosis”. According to World Health Organisation, tuberculosis causes the death of the largest number of people at present time. In India, each year approx. 4-5 lakhs deaths are reported due to tuberculosis, which is about a third of the world’s toll.

questions.subject: General Science

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guerin) vaccine is used for the prevention of tuberculosis (T.B.). It should proculate just after the birth of a baby to prevent T.B.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Typhoid and cholera are typical examples of –
questions.explanation: Typhoid and cholera are typical examples of waterborne diseases. Waterborne diseases are transmitted through water. The interruption of transmission is achieved by proper treatment of drinking water. Almost 4 million people die each year from water related diseases.

questions.subject: General Science

questions.explanation: The liver is major digestive gland which is affected by aflatoxins. Some fungal species of Aspergillus and Penicillium produce aflatoxins that make food toxic.

options.d: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ● The liver is the primary storage site for the malarial parasite (Plasmodium spp.) in the human body. During the life cycle of the parasite, it infects and multiplies within the liver cells (hepatocytes) before moving on to infect red blood cells. ● While the spleen filters the blood and removes infected red blood cells, it's not the primary storage site for the parasite.

questions.explanation: Moniliasis is a disease of the alimentary tract of chickens, turkey, and sometimes other birds. The cause is the fungal yeast, Candida albicans, and the condition is seen worldwide. Morbidity and mortality is usually low. The route of infection is normally oral.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Thalassemia' is a hereditary disease affecting

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Thalassemia is an inherited blood disorder caused when the body does not make enough of a protein called haemoglobin. When there is not enough haemoglobin, the body's red blood corpuscles (RBCs) do not function properly and they last shorter periods of time, so there are fewer healthy red blood corpuscles traveling in the bloodstream. So this condition can cause anemia.

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In respect of women, men can suffer more of colour blindness because-

options.a: They pass more through mental tensions
options.b: They live out of home relatively more

questions.explanation: Colour blindness is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The genes are located on the X-chromosome which is one of the two sex chromosomes. In males (who have only one X-chromosome) one genetic change in each cell is sufficient to cause the condition. Males are affected by X-linked recessive disorders much more frequently than females (who have two X-chromosomes) in which a genetic change would have to occur on both copies of the chromosome to cause the disorder. A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that father cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons. VI. Deficiency, Non-Contagious and Other Diseases 1. Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1. Anorexia : Sleep disorder 2. Insomnia : Eating disorder

questions.question: The malfunctioning of thyroid gland is due to the deficiency of :

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The malfunctioning of thyroid gland is due to the deficiency of iodine. Goitre is an abnormal enlargement of thyroid gland, the most common cause of which is lack of iodine in diet. Deficiency of iodine leads to decreased production of thyroxine and triiodothyronine hormones from the thyroid gland which are necessary to regulate metabolic rate and other vital body functions.

questions.subject: General Science

options.d: More than one of the above

questions.subject: General Science

options.d: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Methemoglobinemia (MetHb) is a blood disorder in which an abnormal amount of methemoglobin is produced. The most common cause of methemoglobinemia is the ingestion or inhalation of oxidizing agents such as nitrates or nitrites.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The radiations used in the treatment of muscle ache are :

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Infrared radiations are used in the treatment of muscle ache. Infrared light is one of several innovative therapies that are being trialed for the management of patients with acute or chronic pain. Infrared light radiation helps cells regenerate or repair themselves. It has been shown to be effective in the treatment of muscle or joint pain, including muscle spasm and stiffness.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The incubation period of hepatitis B virus is

options.e: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.source_book: Ghatna Chakra BPSC Preview (Purvalokan) 2025 General Studies
questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Oncogenes are associated with –
questions.explanation: An oncogene is a kind of abnormal gene that predisposes cells to develop into cancers. The first oncogene ever identified is termed Sarcoma (SRC) – (Pronounced 'Sarc' as it is short for Sarcoma), discovered in 1970. It is a component of cancer-causing virus in chickens, known as the rous sarcoma virus.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following can cause cancer as well as cure it depending upon its intensity and use?
questions.explanation: Ionized radiation is the factor which can cause cancer as well as cure, depending upon its intensity and use. Photon radiation and particle radiation are the types of ionized radiation used in cancer treatment effectively.

questions.question: The Nobel Prize for developing treatment of Parkinson’s disease was given to:

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

He is best known for his work with the neurotransmitter dopamine and its effects in Parkinson's disease, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2000, together with Eric Kandel and Paul Greengard.

questions.question: Lack of which substance causes diabetes in a person?
questions.explanation: Insulin is a hormone made in the pancreas, that allows our body to use sugar (glucose) from carbohydrates in the food that we eat for energy or to store glucose for future use. Insulin helps to keep blood sugar level from getting too high (hyperglycemia) or too low (hypoglycemia). Lack of Insulin in the body causes diabetes in a person. Diabetes patients have excess urination problem called polyuria.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The most common carrier of communicable diseases is

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

MRI scanners use strong magnetic fields, magnetic field gradients, and radio waves to generate images of the organs in the body. MRI technique does not involve use of ionizing radiation (Gamma rays, X-rays and the higher ultraviolet part of the electromagnetic spectrum), which distinguishes it from CT and PET scans.

options.e: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.question: 1. Aditya L1 Lagrange Point – 1 accessed 6 January 2024. 2. It have seven payload. 3. Aditya L1 has a magnetometer mounted on the deck of the vehicle. 4. Visible Emission Line Coronograph in Aditya L1 will send 1440 photos to Earth every day. Which of the above is/are true ?

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.answer_text: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Aditya L1 is the fi rst space based Indian mission to study the Sun. The spacecraft is placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange point 1 (L1) of the Sun-Earth system on 6 January 2024, which is about 1.5 million km from the Earth. A satellite placed in the halo orbit around the L1 point has the major advantage of continuously viewing the Sun without any occultation/eclipses. The spacecraft carries seven payloads to observe the photosphere, chromosphere and the outermost layers of the Sun (the corona) using electromagnetic and particle and magnetic fi eld detectors. The Aditya-L1 satellite has a magnetometer boom mounted on its deck. Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), the primary payload on board India’s fi rst dedicated scientifi c mission to study the sun, Aditya-L1, will be sending 1,440 images of the sun every day to ground stations.

options.b: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Kerala, Gujarat.
options.c: Bihar, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra
options.d: Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh,

questions.answer_text: Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand
questions.explanation: In August 2010, the then Union Cabinet decided to make six institutes equivalent to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, these States are - Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand. They were established in the year 2012 in Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Jodhpur (Rajasthan), Patna (Bihar), Raipur (Chhattisgarh) and Rishikesh (Uttarakhand). The government has also approved two more new AIIMS. It has been decided to establish them in Rae Bareli in Uttar Pradesh and Raiganj in Uttar Dinajpur in West Bengal. The institute to be set up in Raiganj, West Bengal will be set up in Kalyani city of West Bengal. On 7th October 2015, the Union Cabinet has approved the establishment of 3 new AIIMS under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY). These institutes will be set up in Nagpur (Maharashtra), Mangalagiri (Andhra Pradesh) and Kalyani (West Bengal).

questions.explanation: The Cauvery water dispute is in the states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry. The root of this dispute is the agreement signed between the then Madras Presidency and the princely state of Mysore in the year 1892 and in the year 1924. After independence, Karnataka refused to accede to this agreement saying that Tamil Nadu was given priority in it. Seeing that the dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu could not be resolved mutually, the Central Government constituted the 'Cauvery River' Water Disputes Tribunal in the year 1990. The fi nal decision of the Supreme Court in this dispute came in the year 2018 in which the court declared the Cauvery River as a national asset and upheld the fi nal arrangement made by the CWDT for water sharing.

questions.question: The person who led the agitation in Bihar for the separate state whereby in the year 1911 new provinces Bihar and Odisha were formed was-
questions.explanation: Mahesh Narayan, the editor of ‘Bihar Times’ passed away in 1907. Mahesh Narayan demanded a separate state of Bihar through his newspaper. After the death of Mahesh Narayan, Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha became the leader of this movement. Brahman Narayan, Ali Imam, Mazahrul Haq and Hasan Imam also joined Dr. Sinha. In 1908-09, Bihar provincial conferences were organized demanding creation of a separate province of Bihar. The demand of separate state of Bihar carved out of Bengal was accepted on 12 December, 1911 by the Royal Court at Delhi. On 1 April, 1912 a new province of Bihar came into existence comprising parts of Bihar and Odisha with Patna as it’s capital. On 1 April, 1936 Odisha division was separated from Bihar and declared as a new province.

questions.explanation: The Wahabi Movement, indeed an Islamic revivalist initiative, aimed to return to the original teachings of Islam as practiced during the time of the Prophet Muhammad. It emerged in the early 19th century, primarily through the eff orts of Syed Ahmed Barelvi, who was inspired by the ideas of Abdul Wahhab in Saudi Arabia and Shah Waliullah in Delhi. Barelvi's focus was on purifying Islam from perceived innovations and external infl uences, particularly Western ones. He sought to reestablish a society that refl ected the principles and practices of early Islamic communities. The movement's emphasis on strict monotheism and a return to foundational beliefs played a signifi cant role in shaping Islamic thought in South Asia during that period.

In Gaya district of Bihar, the Kisan Sabha emerged as a major political force- exercising infl uence not just on the district’s peasants, but also on the Congress Movement here.The Kisan Sabha Movement in Bihar, institutionalised by the formation of the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929, led peasants across Bihar in several signifi cant struggles. questions.explanation: During the colonial period in India, various tribes and communities resisted the imposition of exploitative taxation systems introduced by the British. Notable among these were the Santhals of Bihar, who revolted in 1855-56 against oppressive tax policies. Under the leadership of Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, and Bhairava, the Santhals rose up with the sole intention of uprooting the rule of the Dikus once and for all. On the evening of 30th June 1855, over 10,000 Santhal men and women assembled at the Bhognadih village, located in the Sahibganj district of present day Jharkhand, and pledged to rise against the exploitative rule of foreigners.

On the basis of soil characteristics, rainfall, temperature and topography, Bihar is divided into three sub-regions namely North-East, North-West Alluvial Plain and South Bihar Alluvial Plain. The South Bihar alluvial plain is further classifi ed into South-East (A) and South-West (B). The North-West Zone comprises a total of 12 districts. While the North-East zone consists of 8 districts. Total 17 districts are included in the South Bihar alluvium Plain Zone, out of which 6 districts are included in the South-East Zone (A) and 11 districts in the South-West Zone (B). Thus it is clear that most of the districts are included in the North-West zone.

questions.explanation: Soils in Bihar are characterised by loamy and alluvial nature. Soils here are rejuvenated every year by deposition of sand, silt and clay. These depositions are brought by Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra river system every year and spread through fl oods. Soils of Bihar region– Type Region Properties of soil Balthar Kaimur Sandy, calcareous, yellow Tal Patna and Munger Heavy soil Terai Champaran and Kishanganj Sandy, calcareous, brown and light yellow Bhangar Patna, Gaya and Rohtas Acidic and rich in lime Khadar Muzaff arpur, Purnia, Saharsa, Darbhanga and Bhagalpur Dark brown and fertile Bal Sundari Saharsa, East and West Champaran Lime and alkaline Soils of Southern Plain is found between North Ganga plain and Southern plateau and it formed due to the alluvium deposited by Sone, Punpun, and Falgu Rivers. 1. Karail-Kewal Soil : It is heavy clay soil which is characterised by wet paddy lands. It is found in Rohtas to Gaya, Aurangabad, Jahanabad, Munger and Bhagalpur etc. 2. Tal Soil : It is found in backwater belt of Ganga which is spread from Buxar to Banka district. Rabi or spring crops like wheat, khesari, gram, peas, masoor, etc. are harvested. 3. Balthar Soil : It is less fertile and has less water absorption capacity. Maize, jowar, bajra, and gram are chief crops.

questions.question: Two statements are given below, fi rst is Assertion (A) and second is Reason (R), read carefully both- Assertion (A) : Southern Bihar is more developed than Northern Bihar Reason (R) : Development of industries occurred in South Bihar. With respect to both the statements, which of the following is true?

options.a: A and R both are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: A and R both are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true but R is false.
options.d: A is false but R is true.

questions.answer_text: A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation: Southern Bihar i.e. present-day Jharkhand was less developed than Northern Bihar. Under development of Southern Bihar was the main reason for the formation of Jharkhand. Therefore, assertion (A) is incorrect. Southern Bihar has a mineral-rich area. Therefore, mineral-based industries developed more frequently in southern Bihar. Jamshedpur, Dhanbad, Bokaro etc. were major industrial cities of the then Southern Bihar.

options.d: More than one of the above
options.e: None of the above

questions.explanation: Kanwar jheel (lake), as it is locally called, is located 22 km north-west of Begusarai Town in Manjhaul. It is a residual oxbow lake, formed due to meandering of Burhi Gandak River, a tributary of River Ganga. The KanwarTaalor Kabartal Wetland located in Begusarai district, is Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake.It is approximately six times the size of the Bharatpur Sanctuary. In November 2020, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) declared it the fi rst Ramsar site in Bihar.

options.b: R is true but A is false

questions.explanation: According to question, clock gained 8 min time interval in 48 hours The time interval per minutes is achieved in 6 hours.
